**New assertions the rewrite should add (rev 24 adds no signing-order assertion):** `Check_both_signers_are_bound` passes for matching emails and names the
applicant/referee when they differ; the primary fills send `textTabs` for prefill and `Text` for recipients, and the
fallbacks the reverse; `Describe_the_failure` has the seven cases; the secure-data tests stay as `development-agent` left them (they pass).

**Reminders & Escalation** — scheduled daily, plus DocuSign events. Reminders at **3 and 7 days**
(`Setting.ReminderDays`), escalation to the process owner with the applicant's details at **14 days**
(`Setting.EscalationDays`) (FR-043, FR-044). Idempotent: a reminder-sent stamp prevents a duplicate on a
re-run.
**Completion** — on envelope completed, sets Grant status to *Acceptance Signed*, stores the signed PDF in
the SharePoint library and writes its URL to `rev_grant.rev_signedpdfurl` (FR-045). The manual
print-sign-scan route (FR-046) is recorded directly on the Grant record through the Model-Driven App — no
flow, by design, because it is a human-attested exception.

### 5.11 `REV | Finance | Capture Payment`

**AUTHORISED 2026-10-20 (rev 28) as `wbs:8.6`.** Requirements FR-107 to FR-111 and US-026 (SDD Amendment A-12); change
order `CO-010`, scope accepted unbilled; OQ-057 and OQ-058 answered at their defaults. Design: `ADR-081`.
*Previously read (rev 6): OPEN — DEFERRED BY REVIEWER DECISION, 2026-09-09. Unauthorised and unbuilt, no FR, no task id.*

**What it does.** One hop the `wbs:8.3` form cannot make. When finance records a payment as the final one, the grant gets its
final payment date, which starts the six-year retention clock (FR-048, §3.4, ADR-004), the application moves from
"Approved" to "Grant Paid", the grant's own status moves from "Acceptance Signed" to "Paid" (amendment b, FR-113), and the payment itself is marked Issued, **by a table-scope business rule on the Payment, not by this flow** (amendment c). **A final payment must carry a date** (reviewer, 2026-10-20):
the same rule refuses the save without it, on the form and on the server, and the date is the payment's own. When the final mark is withdrawn or the payment is
cancelled, the grant (date and status) and the application go back; the payment's status does not (below). The old description of this flow had
three jobs; they are now split. Recording Provider, Bank Account and Payment rows is the `wbs:8.3` form. The date, the status
are this flow; the Issued mark and the date-required check are the payment rule (amendment c, below). The duplicate re-check is neither (below).

**What it does not do.** Stated so nobody reads it into the flow's name.

1. **The pre-issue duplicate re-check is NOT part of this flow.** It stays with `wbs:8.5` and FR-023 (`CO-010` says so). The
   flow does not call `REV | Duplicate | QBO Check`; §5.4's second call site is not built by `wbs:8.6`.
2. **It writes nothing to the Payment row (amendment c).** Its writes are the Grant's date and status and the Application's status. It reads the saved payment's final mark, date, status and grant, and no amount, method, bank account, provider or QuickBooks reference. *Previously read (rev 28): it wrote `rev_paymentstatus` from Pending to Issued; that write is now the payment rule's.*
3. ~~It does not set the Grant's own status to "Paid".~~ **Retired by amendment b (2026-10-20):** it does, from "Acceptance Signed" only, in the same grant write as the date (below). *Previously read (rev 28 as approved): not done, flagged for the reviewer; FR-107 to FR-111 did not ask for it.*
4. It does not update the Anonymised Statistic amount (§5.13 item 2).
5. **It does not build the paid-grants retention job.** See below.

#### Flow

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A(["A Payment is added, or one of: final mark, date, status, grant changes"]) --> P["Read the saved payment as it is now"]
  P --> B{"Linked to a grant?"}
  B -- No --> C{"Marked final and not cancelled?"}
  C -- Yes --> R["Reason: no grant is linked"]
  C -- No --> Z(["Nothing to apply"])
  B -- Yes --> D["Read the grant, its application, and the latest dated final payment on the grant"]
  D --> E["Target date: that payment's date, or none.<br/>Target grant status: Signed to Paid if a final exists, Paid to Signed if none, otherwise as is"]
  E --> F{"Date or grant status different?"}
  F -- Yes --> G["One grant write: final payment date (or clear) and grant status"]
  F -- No --> H
  G --> H["Target status: Approved to Grant Paid if a final payment exists,<br/>Grant Paid to Approved if none, otherwise leave"]
  H --> I{"Status to change?"}
  I -- Yes --> J["Write the application's status"]
  I -- No --> N
  J --> N{"A reason to report?<br/>(date written but application at another status,<br/>or saved payment final and undated,<br/>or saved payment final and Cancelled)"}
  N -- Yes --> M["Tell finance (Teams) and the process owner (Failure Alert)"]
  N -- No --> Z2(["Done"])
  R --> M
```

*The payment's own Issued mark is not a step of this flow (amendment c). The payment rule sets it inside the save, so the flow reads the payment already Issued and writes nothing to it.* *Previously read: a "saved payment final, not cancelled, dated and Pending" decision and a "write the saved payment's status: Issued" action ran last.*

#### What is true after each save (the decision table)

"Finals" are payments on the grant with the final mark set, a status other than Cancelled (OQ-058) **and a date**. "Target date" is
the latest of their dates (FR-107). A final payment with no date is not a final: it starts no clock (`ADR-081` item 2). The payment
rule refuses to save one on every write path, pending `A-CP-9`; the row the rule cannot stop is one that pre-dates it, or any row if verification fails (`A-R102`). The flow always lands on the target,
whatever was saved.

| Finals on the grant | Grant's date | Application | Grant's date becomes | Application becomes | Reported (FR-111) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 or more | empty or different | Approved | target date | Grant Paid | No |
| 1 or more | the target date | Approved | unchanged | Grant Paid (finishes a half-applied run) | No |
| 1 or more | empty or different | Grant Paid | target date | unchanged | No |
| 1 or more | the target date | Grant Paid | unchanged | unchanged — **a repeat save, FR-109** | No |
| 1 or more | empty or different | any other status | target date | unchanged | **Yes — the status is named** |
| 1 or more | the target date | any other status | unchanged | unchanged | No (reported when the date was written) |
| none | set | Grant Paid | cleared | Approved | No |
| none | set | Approved | cleared | unchanged | No |
| none | set | any other status | cleared | unchanged | **Yes — the status is named** |
| none | empty | Grant Paid | unchanged | Approved (finishes a half-applied reversal) | No |
| none | empty | any other status | unchanged | unchanged — **a non-final instalment, FR-109** | No |
| any, **no grant linked** | — | — | none | none | **Yes, only if marked final and not cancelled** |
| any; **the saved payment is final, not cancelled and has no date** | as above, from the other payments | as above | as above, from the other payments | as above | **Yes — "final payment has no date"** |
| any; **the saved payment is final and Cancelled** (FR-112) | as above, from the other payments | as above | as above (it does not count, OQ-058) | as above | **Yes — "cancelled payment is marked final"**, informational |

**The grant's own status, `rev_status` (amendment b, FR-113).** It is decided from the grant's status and from whether a final exists, never from the application's status, so the two rows above and the rows below are independent (a Withdrawn application can sit beside a grant that becomes Paid). It travels in the grant's one write (below).

| Finals on the grant | Grant status | Grant status becomes | Reported (FR-111) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 or more | 3 Acceptance Signed | **4 Paid** (also finishes a half-applied run, where the date already matches) | No |
| 1 or more | 4 Paid | unchanged — **a repeat save, FR-109** | No |
| 1 or more | 1 Awarded or 2 Acceptance Issued | unchanged — never skips a step it has not reached (OQ-060) | **Yes, when the date is written in this run — the status is named** |
| none | 4 Paid | **3 Acceptance Signed** (also finishes a half-applied reversal) | No |
| none | 3 | unchanged — **a non-final instalment, FR-109** | No |
| none | 1 or 2 | unchanged | **Yes, when the date is cleared in this run — the status is named** |

The report on 1 or 2 is tied to the date being written, as the application's is (row 6 of the table above), so a later save of an unrelated instalment does not repeat it. **Wording difference with FR-113 (plan-agent):** the plan lists "Paid already" among the statuses that are reported. Read literally that reports every repeat save of a paid grant, which contradicts FR-109 in the same sentence; the design treats Paid with a final as a silent repeat (second row).

What happens to the **saved payment's own status** is not this flow's doing (amendment c). The payment rule (below) sets it, in the same save and before the flow runs; the flow reads the result and writes nothing to the Payment. For the decision table above it makes no difference: finals are counted by *not Cancelled* and *dated*, never by Issued.

| The saved payment | Its status becomes (by the rule, not the flow) |
|---|---|
| Final, dated, **Pending** | **Issued**, in that same save |
| Final, dated, already Issued or Cleared | unchanged — the rule's condition is Pending only |
| Cancelled, whatever else is set | unchanged — the rule never matches a Cancelled payment; the flow reports it if it is also marked final (FR-112) |
| Not final | unchanged — an instalment is not touched |
| Final and undated | **the save is refused** (rule branch a), so nothing is written; a row that pre-dates the rule stays as it is and the flow reports it |
| Final mark **removed** from a payment that is Issued | **unchanged — never reverted to Pending** (below) |

A final payment that cannot be written at all (the platform refuses the grant's date or status, or the application's status) is not a table row. It is the
flow failing, and it takes the failure path: `REV | Ops | Failure Alert` tells the process owner and the run shows Failed.

#### The grant's own status (amendment b, FR-113)

Ground truth read 2026-10-20, each against source and not against this document.

1. **The column is `rev_grant.rev_status`.** `rev_grantstatus` is the name of the *global option set* (`OptionSets/rev_grantstatus.xml`: 1 Awarded, 2 Acceptance Issued, 3 Acceptance Signed, 4 Paid), not a column; the flow writes `item/rev_status`. Value 4 is already in source, so no option-set change and no import prerequisite (`C-TECH-050`).
2. **Field security: none.** `rev_status` has `IsSecured=0` (`Entities/rev_grant/Entity.xml`, its description says why) and appears in no profile in `Other/FieldSecurityProfiles.xml`. The earlier note was right. The write is a plain write through `REV Service Automation`'s Write on Grant (§6.2); no profile permission or member is added, and `A-CP-7` is not extended.
3. **Triggers on Grant: none can fire from this write.** The only flow with a trigger on `rev_grant` is `REV | Acceptance | Create Envelope`, `message: 1` (Create), so an update starts nothing. This flow's own trigger is on `rev_payment`, so writing the grant starts no further run of it either.
4. **The two acceptance flows that write grant status cannot be overwritten by it, and cannot overwrite it.** `REV | Acceptance | Completion` writes 3 only behind a guard that the grant's status is still 2, so it cannot pull a Paid grant back to 3; `Create Envelope` writes 2 only on the grant's creation; `Reminders & Escalation` selects `rev_status eq 2`, so a Paid grant is never reminded or escalated. Nothing else in `Workflows/`, the saved queries or the code apps writes or filters on grant status (grepped).
5. **Where the status travels.** One `UpdateOnlyRecord` on `rev_grant` carries `item/rev_finalpaymentdate` (the target date or null) and `item/rev_status` (the target status). It runs when **either** differs from what the grant read returned (the read's `$select` gains `rev_status`). The write always carries a status, and when the target is no move (`newGrantStatus` 0) it carries **the value the read returned, whatever it is** (1, 2, 3 or 4), so a date-only change **echoes the current status unchanged**. That is the cost of one write, and it is `A-R103`'s narrow race. Target status: with a dated final, 3 becomes 4 and any other status stays; with none, 4 becomes 3 and any other status stays. **The flow never changes a grant to 1 or 2:** a grant read at 1 or 2 is written back at 1 or 2, an echo and not a transition, and no write ever carries 1 or 2 for a grant that was not already there. *Previously read (rev 28, amendment b as first recorded): "The flow never writes 1 or 2." That contradicted the echo in the previous sentences; the intended meaning was the one above.*
6. **Order.** Grant write (date and status together), then the application's status; the payment's Issued mark is no longer a step of the flow (amendment c). Date and grant status can no longer be half-applied against each other; the half-applied states left are the ones the table already names, and the next save of any payment on the grant finishes them.
7. **Hand-set values.** The same shape as `A-R100`: a grant hand-set to Paid with no payment marked final returns to Acceptance Signed on the next save of any payment on it.

#### As built: three differences from this design, each decided (amendment b, 2026-10-20)

Read from the shipped flow (`Workflows/REVFinanceCapturePayment-8F1C2A44-1013-4B7A-9E21-0A1B2C3D4E13.json`), not from the Dev Summary. The Dev Summary lists a fourth (status in the same write as the date); that is this design, not a difference.

1. **Reasons are one `Compose` of `if()` fragments, not a variable and its setters. ACCEPTED.** The design said "a reason variable and its setters" (`ADR-081` item 5 and the size line); the outcome is identical (one string, empty when nothing is to report), with fewer actions and no `SetVariable`. The wording above is rewritten; the rule that the reason carries references and never an amount, bank detail, date or name is unchanged and applies to every fragment.
2. **The reads run with an all-zero id when no grant is linked, so there is no no-grant branch. ACCEPTED, on one condition that holds.** The reads are `ListRecords` with a `$filter`, and a filter on an id that matches no row returns an empty list; it does not fail, which a single-row `GetItem` would. The date write is gated by `linked` (`dateDiffers` is false for an unlinked payment), so nothing is written to a grant that is not there, and the reason for an unlinked final payment is a fragment of the same `Compose`. The flow diagram's "no grant is linked" branch is therefore a decision inside the reason, not a path. Test `ac9` covers it.
3. **The Warning alert is called before the Teams message. ACCEPTED.** The design fixed no order. Alert first means the process owner learns the reason when the Teams post fails. Cost, stated: the Teams post runs only if the alert succeeded, so a failed alert call also silences Teams; the run then takes the failure path (FR-111) and shows Failed, and the writes have already been made.

#### Trigger, identity and connections

- **Trigger:** `When_a_payment_is_recorded_or_changed` — `SubscribeWebhookTrigger` on `rev_payment`, `message: 4` (Added or
  Modified, read live from `stringmap` 2026-08-28, `knowledge/technology/power-automate.md`), `scope: 4`, `runas: 3`,
  `filteringattributes: rev_isfinalpayment,rev_paymentdate,rev_paymentstatus,rev_grantid`, outputs secured, concurrency 1.
  Delete is not a trigger (`ADR-081` item 1). `A-CP-1`, `A-CP-2`, `A-CP-4`.
- **Run as the flow owner (`svc-grantautomation`), not the person who saved.** The Finance role holds Read and AppendTo on
  Grant and nothing at all on Application (§6.2), so a run as the modifying user could not make either write. The service
  account's `REV Service Automation` role already holds Read and Write on Grant, Application and Payment.
- **Secured columns (re-checked 2026-10-20, amendment c).** The flow no longer writes any `REV_FinanceOnly` column: its writes are the Grant's `rev_finalpaymentdate` and `rev_status` and the Application's `rev_status`. It still **reads** the Payment's final mark, date, status and grant as the flow owner, through its team's membership of `REV_FinanceOnly` (Read, Update and Create all *Allowed*, `Other/FieldSecurityProfiles.xml`), and still writes `rev_finalpaymentdate`, which is in `REV_TrusteeRestricted` with the same Allowed flags and the same team as a member, in all three settings files. **No privilege, profile permission or profile member is added.** `A-CP-7` is narrowed to those two acts. The write to `rev_paymentstatus` is now made by the payment rule under the saving user (below). *Previously read (rev 28): the Issued write was the flow's first write to a `REV_FinanceOnly` column, a secured write through team membership that no shipped flow performed on `rev_payment`.*
- **Connections:** the two connection references the solution already has, `rev_SharedDataverse` and `rev_SharedTeams`. No new
  connector, no new reference.
- **Audit (changed by amendment c).** The grant's date and status and the application's status are audited columns; those writes are attributed to the service account. The Payment row is no longer written by the flow, so its `modifiedby` and its status change are attributed to **the finance user who saved it**, and the rule's Issued set sits in the same save as the tick. `rev_payment` is audit-enabled (`Entity.xml`, `dev-auditing-settings.json`). Whether the audit history records a column set by a server-side rule is `A-CP-9` check 4. *Previously read (rev 28): after the Issued write the Payment's `modifiedby` read the service account, and who ticked it stayed in the audit history.*

#### Idempotency, ordering and the loop (FR-109)

The flow computes the target from the payments that exist, and writes only what differs. A second save of the same payment,
a save of a different payment on the same grant, and a run replayed from run history all find current equals target and write
nothing. Concurrency is 1, so two saves on one grant are processed one after the other and the later run reads everything the
earlier one wrote. The writes are separate calls and run in a fixed order: the grant (date and status together), then the application's status. A run that stops between them leaves the grant done and the application at Approved, and the next save of any payment on that grant finishes the job (table rows 2 and 10). **A final payment reading Pending is no longer a sign about the flow:** the payment rule makes it Issued in the save itself, so a final, dated payment reading Pending means the rule did not run (`A-CP-9`, `A-R104`), not that the flow stopped.

**The flow writes nothing to the Payment, so it cannot start itself (amendment c).** Its trigger is on `rev_payment`; its writes are to `rev_grant` and `rev_application`. There is no self-edge and no extra run. `rev_paymentstatus` stays in the trigger's filter on purpose: cancelling a payment, or un-cancelling one, must recompute the grant (FR-110, OQ-058). The one write that does touch it, the payment rule's Issued set, is made inside the person's own save, so one save is one run. The loop check `NoTriggerLoop` (`src/tests/narrative/test_solution_flows.py`) and the Solution Checker's `flow-avoid-recursive-loop` have nothing to reject for this flow. `A-CP-8` (the extra run) is **withdrawn**. *Previously read (rev 28): the flow's own Pending-guarded Issued write started a second run that ended on a fixed-point argument, at the cost of one no-op run per final payment (`A-CP-8`). Build 20261020-4 was blocked because the repository's loop check ignores trigger conditions and has no guarded-self-edge mechanism; the reviewer removed the write rather than add one.*

#### The payment's status, and what undoes it (FR-110)

The **payment rule** moves a payment **Pending to Issued** when Final is Yes, and nothing else; the flow writes nothing to the Payment. Neither writes Cleared (the bank's act) or Cancelled, and **nothing ever writes Pending**. So:

- **Unticking Final** on an Issued payment reverses the grant and the application (FR-110) and leaves the payment Issued. Whether
  the money went out is a fact the flow cannot see; guessing Pending would be wrong the day a payment was issued and merely
  mis-marked. If it was not sent, finance sets the status by hand. The status is the payment's own record; the grant's date and
  the application's status are what the flow keeps in line.
- **Cancelling** a final payment is a status finance sets. It stops counting (OQ-058), the grant and the application revert, the
  flow does not write the payment, and it reports the case as FR-112 words it (an informational message; one more finance message per cancellation of a final payment, which the
  plan's text asks for and the design would otherwise have left silent).
- **Un-cancelling** a final, dated payment back to Pending makes it final and Pending, so the rule marks it Issued in that save. A finance user
  who wants a final payment to stay Pending unticks Final: under answer 3, a final payment is an issued one.
- **Correcting the date** of an Issued final payment re-records the grant's date and does not touch the payment's status.

#### The payment rule: date required, and the Issued mark (reviewer answer 3; amendment c)

**One business rule on `rev_payment`, scope Entity, replacing both the flow's Issued write and the form-scope "date required" rule** (`ADR-081` items 7 and 8; reviewer decision *"4"*, 2026-10-20). Microsoft Learn (`data-platform-create-business-rule`, read 2026-10-20) states that Entity scope means "Model-driven app forms and server", that set column value and show error message are available at table scope (set requirement level is form-only), and that server-side rules are generated as synchronous plug-ins. Its error-handling page (`handle-exceptions-code`, "Custom errors from business rules") states that a server-evaluated rule's error message reaches the caller as an exception. One condition chain:

| Branch | Condition | Action | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| a | Final = Yes **and** Payment Date is empty | **Show Error Message** on Payment Date: a payment date is required when the payment is marked final | Refuses the save on the form and on an API or import write; closes `A-R102` by design, pending `A-CP-9` |
| b | not (a), **and** Final = Yes **and** Payment Status = Pending | **Set column value:** Payment Status = Issued | FR-112: the same save makes the payment Issued, so the flow need not |

It touches only Pending, and only to Issued: it never matches Cancelled, Issued or Cleared and never writes Pending. Set requirement level is not used (form-only); the error message is the requirement, and the only form of it that holds server-side. On the form the rule also runs in the browser, so the error shows beside the field and the status turns to Issued as soon as Final is ticked. Because the Entity rule covers the form, **no separate form-scope rule is authored**. The rule is authored in the DEV maker designer and exported into source, never written as workflow XAML by hand (`ADR-081` item 8 stands); the exported file is checked in source and may be changed afterwards only by a small edit as defined in `ADR-081` item 8, amendment d, which closes only after a DEV import and the `A-CP-9` checks it affects (`A-CP-9`).

Points the reviewer's decision needed settled (read 2026-10-20):

1. **Cancelled and Final.** Branch b cannot touch a Cancelled payment, by its condition. Branch a does apply to one: a payment that is Final, Cancelled and undated cannot be saved until it is dated or Final is unticked. That is the rule as decided, not a defect: a payment marked final should carry a date whatever its status. The flow's FR-112 report for a cancelled final payment is unchanged. Not narrowed; a Cancelled exclusion on branch a is the one-line alternative if the reviewer wants it, and nothing waits on it.
2. **Same-save order with the flow.** Ticking Final on a dated Pending payment is one save carrying Final = Yes and status Pending; the rule adds Issued inside it. The flow starts after the save (a row trigger runs after the operation: argued, not read from a page) and **reads the payment again by id** (`Get_the_saved_payment`), never the status from the trigger body, so it reads Issued. It would reach the same grant date, grant status and application status if it read Pending: **the flow's target depends on Final, date and not-Cancelled only, never on Issued** (decision table). So the answer does not depend on the rule's pipeline stage, which no page read here states, and the trigger fires on the tick in any case (final mark, date and grant are in its filter). The rule's set does not start a second run.
3. **Who saves, and field security.** `rev_paymentstatus`, `rev_isfinalpayment` and `rev_paymentdate` are `REV_FinanceOnly` columns with identical permissions (Read, Update, Create all Allowed). The profile has exactly two member teams: Finance and `REV Service Accounts`. A user who can write Final = Yes through column security can therefore also write Payment Status, so the rule's set cannot be refused for anyone who reaches branch b. A user outside the profile cannot write Final at all. `svc-grantautomation` is a member and, after this amendment, writes nothing to Payment; a future flow that did would fire the rule under that identity. **Not measured:** whether the rule's set runs under the saving user's column permissions or the platform's own context. It does not matter for these two teams (both Allowed); `A-CP-9` check 3 observes the first non-member save so that it is seen to fail cleanly, not guessed.
4. **Existing rows.** A rule runs on a save, not on stored rows (Learn FAQ). A row that pre-dates it is changed only at its next save, and branch a refuses that save until the row is dated. PRD has no payments before the flow is live (`A-R100` listing).
5. **Audit.** The payment's `modifiedby` and status change are the saving user's (see "Audit" above).

*Previously read (rev 28 as approved): a form-scope rule making Payment Date business required when Final is Yes, plus a flow write of Issued; "API and import writes are not stopped by the form, and no plug-in is added", the flow's report being the backstop (`A-R102`). Still rejected: a column-level required setting (unconditional; blocks a Pending payment with no date, which `wbs:8.3` allows) and a plug-in (a new component class outside `CO-010`; a business rule is no assembly, no signing, no deployment).*

**The flow's backstop stays.** An undated final payment is still not counted as final, starts no clock and is reported ("final payment has no date"), as a defence for rows that pre-date the rule and for any write if verification fails. It costs one fragment of the reasons `Compose` and spares the design from trusting a platform behaviour nobody here has seen.

#### Visibility when a final payment cannot be applied (FR-111)

One message, built once, sent to **finance** (Teams, to `rev_FinanceAlertUpn`) and to the **process owner** (the existing
`REV | Ops | Failure Alert` child flow: an Error Log row at severity Warning and the process owner's Teams card). It carries the
payment reference (`PAY-…`), the grant reference (`REV-…`), the reason in plain words, and what to do. **It carries no amount,
bank detail, date, name or note** (NFR-012, NFR-150). The report is the last step, after the writes, so a failure to send it
never undoes them. If `rev_FinanceAlertUpn` is blank the Teams post fails, the run takes the failure path and the process
owner is alerted; **finance is told nothing**. The variable is therefore `isrequired=1` with no default (§12). **Today finance
and the process owner are one person, so that person receives two messages for one cause**, one from each route. That is accepted
for now and is the cost of keeping the variable separate for when the roles split.

**Restart route (not retry).** FR-111 forbids a background retry and the flow has none; the platform's own transient-error
retry on each action is unchanged. Finance corrects the cause and saves the payment again. **A save that changes none of the
four trigger columns sends no update and so does not start the flow.** The message therefore says: untick Final payment, save,
tick it again, save. Both saves are safe (FR-109, FR-110). For a payment with no date the message instead says: add the date and
save. Where the cause is the application's status, nothing finance can do changes it and the message is informational.

#### Paid-grants retention job — stays out of this task, flagged

Dev Summary §3.2 records the six-year paid-grants job as *"not implementable in this release"*, because it needs
`rev_finalpaymentdate`. **It is not in `CO-010` and this revision does not add it.** What `wbs:8.6` changes: the date will
exist, and the Dev Summary's sentence *"No Phase 1 application can reach Grant Paid"* stops being true in each environment on
the day this flow is activated there. What it does not change: no record can be six years from its final payment before six
years after the first final payment is recorded, so the job's absence over-retains nothing for years. The exposure is a date
in the diary, not a live breach. The job targets `rev_grant`, needs a join to its application and is applied by a
tenant administrator (§6, §12); `ensure-bulk-delete-jobs.ps1` is the evidence for `wbs:0.7`. **Whether it belongs to
`wbs:0.7` or needs its own change order is for `pm-agent` and `commercial-agent`**, and the Dev Summary row is
`development-agent`'s to update when the flow ships.

> **Rev 31:** designed in `ADR-083` item 1, under `wbs:0.7`, at the reviewer's instruction to build it with the other
> retention jobs (D-1, 2026-10-22). It deletes `rev_application`, joined to `rev_grant` for the date, not `rev_grant`
> itself (the paragraph above said it *targets* `rev_grant`). The paragraph's urgency reading still holds: the first
> deletion is six years after the first final payment.

#### Size

About **28 actions** in one scope (amendment c removes the Issued guard and its write: the shipped file's 27 plus the trigger becomes about 25 plus the trigger, for development-agent to recount), nested no more than four levels (amendment b adds one Compose for the target grant status and one widened condition; no new read and no new write). Four reads (the saved payment, the grant, the application, the latest dated
final payment), two writes (grant date and status in one, application status), the reasons as one `Compose` of conditional fragments, one report block, the failure path.
The undated-payment read of the earlier design is gone. **Judgement:** proportionate for two writes and their reversal. The set-and-clear, the grant's Signed/Paid-and-back and
the application's Approved/Grant Paid-and-back paths are each one computed target, not two branches.

**Serves** `wbs:8.6` (`CO-010`), after `wbs:8.1`, `8.3` and `8.4`: FR-107, FR-108, FR-109, FR-110, FR-111, FR-112, FR-113; US-026 (AC-1 to AC-19).

### 5.12 `REV | Retention | Retention & Erasure Helper`

Three modes. The **native recurring bulk-delete jobs are the primary retention control** (ADR-004); modes 1 and 2 of
this flow are the residual that covers only what the native job cannot reach, and mode 3 answers a subject access
request. **Not built** (measured 2026-10-22: none of the 13 flow definitions in source is a Retention flow); `wbs:0.7`
(§4.2 item 14).

**Rev 33 (`ADR-088`): mode 3 (SAR extract) is decided — started by hand by the process owner, read-only.** It is no
longer a proposal. *Previously read (rev 1 to rev 32): "Two confirmed modes plus one proposed mode … Mode 3 (SAR
extract) is a proposal, not an agreed design". Previously read (rev 33 first draft, corrected by the reviewer the same
day): "mode 3 (SAR extract) is withdrawn. A SAR is a documented manual procedure … not a mode of this flow".*
**QuickBooks:** this flow cannot write to it (read-only, `ADR-017`); the financial record stays out of erasure until the
finance period ends, and **Finance deletes it after six years by a process outside this solution** (`ADR-088` item 6).

**How the helper ships.** A Power Automate cloud flow has exactly one trigger (measured: each of the 13 definitions in
source has one), and the modes start three different ways, so the helper is one design shipped as more than one flow
definition. **Mode 3 is its own definition**, `REV | Retention | Retention & Erasure Helper (SAR extract)`. That makes
its read-only property checkable from source: the definition contains no delete action and no update of any business
table. The **locate step** is a child flow, `REV | Retention | Retention & Erasure Helper (locate)`, called by mode 2
and mode 3, so both find the same rows from the same applicant; child flows are already used in this solution
(`REV | Ops | Failure Alert`). **Rev 34 (`ADR-089`): modes 1 and 2 are their own definitions too**, and a fifth, the
*snapshot* child, writes the Not Granted snapshot for modes 1 and 2 (§5.12.4). *Previously read: "How modes 1 and 2 are
packaged is decided with the helper's build; neither can share mode 3's trigger."*

**Mode 3, specified (rev 33, `ADR-088` item 1).** Serves FR-053, `wbs:0.13` from rev 34 (`CO-011`; previously `wbs:0.7`) (QuickBooks step: depends on `wbs:7.1`).

|---|---|

Identity is confirmed **before** the run (§4.2 item 5) |

| **Writes** | Only: one extract file and the PDF copies in the SAR folder, path from the new environment variable `rev_SpoSarFolderUrl` (`A-SAR-7`, `A-SAR-9`); one evidence-log row (§4.2 item 9; the actor from the trigger, `A-SAR-8`); one Teams message to the process owner with the reference and file name only; **under delivery option B** (§4.2 item 8, selected by `A-SAR-4`), one protected email from the service mailbox to the requester's email on record with the extract attached, sent with no human review (`A-R108`). **No delete action and no update of any business table** |

| **Failure** | One scope per store, so one unreachable store (for example QuickBooks before `wbs:7.1`) writes a "not read, and why" line in its section instead of failing the run; a failure of the run itself calls the Failure Alert child flow (record reference only) and sends no "extract ready" message, so a partial file is never treated as an extract |
| **Size** | About 42 actions in mode 3 (two of them the option B send) plus about 8 in the locate child. **Judgement:** proportionate for nine stores gathered once per request, each in its own scope; the alternative is a second and third person per request, which the reviewer rejected |
| **Depends on** | The helper's evidence-log store (FR-054): **designed in rev 34**, `rev_retentionlog` (§5.12.3); not in source yet (measured: not among the 15 tables). *Previously read: "designed with the helper's build"*; the QuickBooks connection (`wbs:7.1`) for the QuickBooks step only; the audit-read privilege on `REV Service Automation` (§12) |

#### 5.12.1 Mode 1, specified (rev 34, `ADR-089` items 2 to 4)

Serves FR-048 (evidence of it), FR-049, FR-054, FR-055, NFR-010, `wbs:0.13` (`CO-011`, approved). Definition:
`REV | Retention | Retention & Erasure Helper (sweep)`.

**What it protects (the property):** every deletion the jobs make is recorded, row by row, with no personal data; no
copy of a deleted case survives outside Dataverse; no application is deleted without the snapshot FR-055 needs; a job
that stops deleting is noticed. The steps below are one way of meeting it.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Trigger** | Recurrence, **weekly, Monday 00:30 UTC** (`Recurrence` is already used by three definitions in source). Weekly, not monthly, because the jobs' day of the month is whichever day the provisioning script first ran in each environment (`ensure-bulk-delete-jobs.ps1` schedules the next free `startTimeUtc`), so mode 1 cannot be aligned to it. **Why 8 days of look-ahead:** an application whose clock passes on or before the next job run is always seen by at least one weekly run first. It is a format constant of the weekly schedule, not a tunable |
| **Runs as** | The service identity |
| **1. Pre-pass** | Three `ListRecords` with the jobs' own rules, the clock moved 8 days ahead: Grant Paid (11) whose grant's `rev_finalpaymentdate` is older than 72 months; Rejected (8) whose `rev_decisiondate` is older than 12 months; Withdrawn (9) or Incomplete (10) whose applicant's `rev_lastcontactdate` is older than 6 months. Rules read from the same periods as `dataverse.bulkDeleteJobs` (§3.4.1); a test holds the two equal. Each application already logged as *Scheduled* is skipped, so a weekly re-run writes nothing twice |
| **2. Snapshot** | For each new application: call the snapshot child (§5.12.4). It writes a Not Granted snapshot only where §5.13 step 3 says so; otherwise it writes nothing |
| **3. Log** | One `rev_retentionlog` row per application: run type *Retention sweep*, `rev_recordreference` = the application reference, data type *Application (with Review, Grant, Payment)*, rule (paid 6 years, rejected 12 months, withdrawn or incomplete 6 months), `rev_scheduledon` = the date its clock passes, outcome *Scheduled*, and the signed PDF's server-relative path if the grant has one (it is named with the grant reference `GR-yyyy-nnnnn`, never a name). If the applicant has no other application that is not itself due, a second row for the applicant reference, rule *Orphaned applicant*, data type *Applicant (with Bank Account)* |
| **4. Reconcile** | Every *Scheduled* row whose date has passed: look the reference up. **Gone:** delete the signed PDF at the logged path (SharePoint *Delete file*, `A-ERA-3`), set outcome *Deleted* and `rev_actionedon`. **Still there 35 days after its date:** set outcome *Overdue*, so a job that has stopped is visible within five weeks (NFR-010). An applicant row that is still there because a new application arrived is set *Not due*, not *Overdue* |
| **5. Stale open cases** (first run of each month, decision D4) | `ListRecords` of applications in statuses 1 to 7 whose applicant's `rev_lastcontactdate` is older than `RetentionStaleCaseMonths` (new `rev_setting` key, default 12). Listed by reference for the process owner to close (Withdrawn or Rejected), which puts them on a job's clock. Mode 1 never changes a status itself (`A-R110`) |
| **6. Report** | One Teams message to the process owner: counts scheduled, deleted and overdue, and the references of overdue and stale cases. No names |
| **Writes** | `rev_retentionlog` (create, update); `rev_anonymisedstatistic` (create, through the child); SharePoint *Delete file* in the signed-acceptance library. **No Dataverse delete** |
| **Failure** | Each of steps 1 to 5 in its own scope; a failed scope calls Failure Alert (record reference only) and the next week's run picks up the same rows, because every step is idempotent on the log |
| **Size** | **About 33 actions.** *Judgement:* proportionate — a record of every deletion, the PDF clean-up and a job watchdog, each a short loop |
| **Not done here, and why** | Dataverse deletes (the jobs, `ADR-004`); orphaned applicants (the `orphanedApplicants` job, §3.4.1); DocuSign envelopes (the account's document retention setting, decision D1, §12); QuickBooks (Finance, `ADR-088` item 6); `msdyn_aievent` (its own PRD job, `ADR-083`). *Previously read (rev 1 to rev 33): monthly, "Delete orphaned Applicant rows" and "Purge matching DocuSign envelopes" as steps of mode 1* |

#### 5.12.2 Mode 2, specified (rev 34, `ADR-089` items 5 to 8)

Serves FR-051, FR-052, FR-054, FR-055, `wbs:0.13` (`CO-011`, approved). Definition:
`REV | Retention | Retention & Erasure Helper (erasure)`.

**What it protects (the property):** after a run, nothing about the person remains in any store this solution writes,
except what a stated hold keeps, and the requester is told what is kept, why and until when; the run cannot start by a
slip of the menu.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Trigger** | Dataverse *When a row is selected* on `rev_applicant` from the Grant Administration app's **Flow** menu, as mode 3, with **one text input: the applicant reference, typed** (`A-ERA-1`). A mismatch stops the run before anything is read. The process owner checks the requester's identity and that the request is an erasure **before** the run (runbook, §4.2 item 5); if a SAR was asked too, mode 3 runs first (§4.2 item 1) |
| **Runs as** | The service identity |
| **1. Locate** | The locate child (rev 33): the applicant and every application, review, grant, payment and bank account linked to it |
| **2. Hold rule** (decision D2, approved: *"It only erases when final payment is checked."*) | **A case with a grant is erased only when every grant has its final payment recorded (`rev_finalpaymentdate` set); otherwise the run stops.** A case with no grant is unaffected. On a stop the run logs one row, outcome *Retained (hold)*, emails the requester from the service mailbox (fixed runbook wording: the request is held until the grant's final payment is recorded, and why) and tells the process owner, who runs mode 2 again after the final payment. *As presented: stop only if a grant had a signed acceptance and no final payment date.* Nothing is deleted. No other hold is evaluated by the flow; a legal claim or dispute is the process owner's judgement before the trigger (runbook) |
| **3. Snapshot** | The snapshot child, for each application (§5.12.4) |
| **4. Log, before deleting** | One `rev_retentionlog` row per record: run type *Erasure*, reference, data type, rule *Erasure request*, outcome *Scheduled*. Written first, so a run that fails half-way leaves evidence of what it was doing |
| **5. Capture the reply address** | The applicant's `rev_email` into a variable with secure inputs and outputs, because the row is about to go |
| **6. Delete the copies outside Dataverse** | Each grant's signed PDF (`rev_signedpdfurl`, SharePoint *Delete file*, `A-ERA-3`); every service-mailbox message to or from the applicant's address, and every message to or from the referee's address whose subject carries this application's reference (Outlook search, `A-SAR-12`; Outlook *Delete email*, `A-ERA-4`) |
| **7. Delete the case** | One Dataverse *Delete a row* on `rev_applicant`; the parental cascades remove applications, reviews, grants, payments and bank accounts (§3.3). Needs delete privileges on `REV Service Automation` that it does not hold today (measured 2026-10-22: it deletes only `rev_provider`), `A-ERA-2` |
| **8. Outcomes** | Each log row to *Deleted*; a QuickBooks row per paid grant, outcome *Retained (finance)*, `rev_retaineduntil` = final payment date + 6 years; an *Audit history* row per decision D3 |
| **9. Tell the requester** (FR-052) | `SendEmailV2` from the service mailbox to the captured address: the application references deleted; that the payment record in QuickBooks is kept under the finance policy until the date above and then deleted by Finance; that DocuSign keeps a signed envelope until its retention setting purges it (D1), if one is younger; the `msdyn_aievent` statement (PRD, at most 30 days); the audit statement (D3); that the website may hold a copy, which Revitalise handles separately (`A-R107`). Fixed wording from the runbook, dates computed; no case content |
| **10. Notify** | `SendEmailV2` to the `ErasureNotificationEmail` setting (new `rev_setting` key, the DPO's mailbox; §6.6: *"the DPO is notified"*), references only. Teams message to the process owner: references, and any DocuSign envelope still in progress, which she voids by hand (the connector has no void action in source) |
| **Writes** | `rev_retentionlog`; `rev_anonymisedstatistic` (through the child); one Dataverse delete; SharePoint and Outlook deletes; two emails; one Teams message |
| **Failure** | Steps 6 and 7 in one scope; a failure before step 7 leaves the case in place with *Scheduled* log rows, and the process owner re-runs (every step is idempotent: a file or message already gone is not an error, `A-ERA-3`, `A-ERA-4`) |
| **Size** | **About 40 actions** (two on the hold path's requester email). *Judgement:* proportionate for a destructive, rare, regulated action: one confirmation, one hold check, one delete of the case, and the reply the law requires |

#### 5.12.3 The retention evidence log, `rev_retentionlog` (rev 34, `ADR-089` item 4)

FR-054: *"log every retention deletion run and every erasure action with the record reference, data type, date and
rule applied, and SHALL hold no personal data in that log"*. Organisation-owned. Audited (§6.5). No column secured.

| Column | Type | Holds |
|---|---|---|
| `rev_name` | Autonumber `RL-{DATETIMEUTC:yyyy}-{SEQNUM:6}` | Row id |
| `rev_runtype` | Choice: Retention sweep, Erasure, SAR extract | Which mode wrote it |
| `rev_recordreference` | Text (40) | `REV-yyyy-nnn`, `REV-A-nnnnn` or `GR-yyyy-nnnnn`. **Text, not a lookup**, so it outlives the row (as `rev_errorlog`, §3.3) |
| `rev_datatype` | Choice: Applicant (with Bank Account), Application (with Review, Grant, Payment), Signed PDF, Mailbox messages, QuickBooks record, Audit history, SAR extract | What was acted on |
| `rev_ruleapplied` | Choice: Paid 6 years, Rejected 12 months, Withdrawn or incomplete 6 months, Orphaned applicant, Erasure request, Hold, SAR access | Why |
| `rev_outcome` | Choice: Scheduled, Deleted, Not due, Overdue, Retained (hold), Retained (finance), Extract written | Result |
| `rev_scheduledon` | Date only | When the clock passes (mode 1) or the run date (modes 2, 3) |
| `rev_actionedon` | Date and time (UTC) | When the outcome was set |
| `rev_retaineduntil` | Date only | For a retained record: until when (FR-052) |
| `rev_signedpdfpath` | Text (400) | The signed PDF's server-relative path, reference-named; cleared once deleted |
| `rev_detail` | Text (400) | Composed by the flow from a fixed list only: the SAR file name (reference and UTC time) and the stores read; never free text from a case |
| `rev_startedby` | Lookup to `systemuser` | Who started an erasure or a SAR (rev 33, `A-SAR-8`). A staff member, never the data subject; empty for mode 1 |

**Who can do what.** `REV Service Automation`: create, read, update (organisation). `REV Admin`: read. Nobody holds
delete; the table is never in a bulk-delete job (D5). **Domain invariants:** the row names no data subject (C-DOM-004);
`rev_detail` is never written from a case column (a unit test over the three definitions' expressions).

#### 5.12.4 The snapshot child, packaging and size (rev 34, `ADR-089` item 1)

**Snapshot child**, `REV | Retention | Retention & Erasure Helper (snapshot)`, input: one application id. If the
application's latest review outcome is Deferred and its status is not Approved (7), Rejected (8) or Grant Paid (11), it
writes one Not Granted `rev_anonymisedstatistic` row with the same fields `REV | Portal | Finalise Decisions` writes
(§5.13 step 3, rev 27); otherwise nothing. **What it cannot do, stated:** check that a snapshot already exists for an
Approved or Rejected application. A snapshot carries no reference by design (§3.3), so existence is unknowable; the
guarantee for decided applications is that Finalise Decisions writes the snapshot in the same run that sets the
decision, and a failure there raises Failure Alert. *Previously read (rev 1 to rev 33): "verifies a snapshot exists
before any record is deleted".* About 7 actions.

| Definition | Trigger | Actions (about) | New since rev 33 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Mode 1 (sweep) | Recurrence, weekly | 33 | yes |
| Mode 2 (erasure) | *When a row is selected* + typed reference | 40 | yes |
| Mode 3 (SAR extract) | *When a row is selected* | 42 | no (rev 33) |
| Locate child | Child flow | 8 | no (rev 33) |
| Snapshot child | Child flow | 7 | yes |
| **Helper total** | | **about 130** | 80 new in rev 34 |

Other components the helper adds, all environments: table `rev_retentionlog` (12 columns, 4 choices, §12.1
prerequisite path, `C-TECH-050`); privileges on `REV Service Automation` — create/read/update `rev_retentionlog`,
create `rev_anonymisedstatistic` (held already), delete on `rev_applicant` and its cascade children (`A-ERA-2`), audit
read (rev 33); `REV Admin` read on `rev_retentionlog`; two `rev_setting` keys, `RetentionStaleCaseMonths` and
`ErasureNotificationEmail`; the DocuSign account's document retention setting (D1, §12). No new connector type,
environment variable or connection reference (SharePoint, Outlook, Teams and Dataverse are in source).

### 5.13 Who writes the Anonymised Statistic snapshot — DERIVED

The source's access matrix says the service account "Writes" the Anonymised Statistic table, but **no flow in
the source's inventory writes it**, and FR-055 requires the statistics to survive deletion of the underlying
personal data. Derived assignment:
1. `REV | Portal | Finalise Decisions` writes the snapshot at decision (outcome = Approved / Deferred /
   Rejected), so reporting is current rather than end-of-life. **Rev 27:** `rev_statisticoutcome` holds only Granted
   and Not Granted. **Reviewer, 2026-10-20 (`Q-FD-3`, §5.7):** no third value; *"deferred means that it has not been
   granted and could be granted in the future."* So a Deferred review writes **no** snapshot, and each application is
   counted once, at its final outcome in a later round: Granted or Not Granted. A deferral never produces a second row
   for the same application.
2. `REV | Finance | Capture Payment` updates the amount on final payment. **Rev 28: not done by the flow as authorised.** FR-107 to FR-111 write a date and a status and the flow reads no amount (§5.11); the snapshot's amount stays as `Finalise Decisions` wrote it. Flagged for the reviewer, not added (`ADR-081` item 9).
3. `REV | Retention | Retention & Erasure Helper` **verifies a snapshot exists before any record is
   deleted** *(rev 34: only the deferred case is checkable; see §5.12.4)* — the safety net that makes FR-055 true even if step 1 failed. **Rev 27:** this is also where an
   application whose last review was Deferred, and which was never decided again, is counted: it has no snapshot, so
   the helper writes one **Not Granted** snapshot before deletion. Specified here for the helper's design (still
   unbuilt); flow #7 does not do it.
The snapshot carries no lookup and no reference number (§3.1), so it is genuinely anonymised and is not
touched by erasure.

### 5.14 `REV | Ops | Failure Alert`

Child flow called from the configured `run after has failed / timed out` path of every other flow. Writes one
`rev_errorlog` row — flow name, run ID, error message, record reference, timestamp, severity — and posts a
Teams alert to the process owner. **Holds no personal data** (NFR-012, NFR-016). Native Power Automate run
history and Dataverse field-change auditing back it up (source §5, Security Model §8).

> ⚠️ **Compliance note on `rev_recordreference`.** The Security Model §3 and the Data Governance Framework §3
> both classify the Error Log as non-personal because it holds "record references only". A reference that
> resolves to a living person is strictly **pseudonymised personal data**, not anonymous. The mitigations
> designed in are: a short 90-day operational retention (derived — the sources say only "short"), Tier 2
> handling with no trustee access, and no name, contact detail or narrative fragment ever written to the
> message. Flagged for DPO confirmation; recorded as risk A-R12.
