### ADR-081: A Payment save makes the grant's final payment date and the application's status match the payments that exist

**Status:** `Accepted` (rev 28, approved 2026-10-20 with three answers folded in, below; items 6 to 8 amended by amendment c, 2026-10-20) · **Date:** 2026-10-20 · **WBS:** `wbs:8.6` (change order `CO-010`,
scope accepted unbilled, not in `contract/wbs.json`) · **Raised by:** SDD Amendment A-12 (FR-107 to FR-112, US-026; FR-112 and OQ-059 added by the reviewer-directed revision), approved 2026-10-20, and the
architect request in `CO-010`'s "Before development can start".

**Context.** The reviewer's decision on the question deferred since 2026-09-09, verbatim: *"Yes, this flow needs to be build. 2- 4 hours of work on a new WBS 8.6.
Non-billable."* (`CO-010`). Ground truth read 2026-10-20: (a) every `rev_payment` column except `rev_name` is `IsSecured=1`, including
`rev_grantid`, `rev_isfinalpayment`, `rev_paymentdate` and `rev_paymentstatus`; (b) `rev_grant.rev_finalpaymentdate` is a DateOnly, secured, audited
column and no flow writes it; (c) `rev_applicationstatus` has "Grant Paid" (11) and no flow in `Workflows/` writes it; **nothing keys on application
status 7 or 11** — no flow filter, no saved query, no code-app source other than a label (grepped); (d) the Finance role has create, read and update on
Payment, Read and AppendTo on Grant and nothing on Application, and no delete on Payment (§6.2); (e) `REV Service Automation` holds write on Grant,
Application and Payment, and the service account's team is a member of `REV_FinanceOnly`; (f) `rev_paymentstatus` is Pending 1, Issued 2, Cleared 3,
Cancelled 4 with default 1; (g) `message: 4` is *Added or Modified* (`stringmap`, read live 2026-08-28), and no flow in this solution uses it;
(h) no flow here writes a null, uses `concurrency` on a row trigger, or filters on `rev_paymentstatus`. SDD A-12's reviewer answers: OQ-057 *"Payment date"*,
OQ-058 *"Correct. All payments marked final."* (i) **Added at the approval:** `REV_FinanceOnly` gives Read, Update and Create *Allowed* on `rev_paymentstatus`, and
`REV Service Accounts` is a member of both `REV_FinanceOnly` and `REV_TrusteeRestricted` in all three settings files; `rev_payment` is audit-enabled; the solution
holds no plug-in, web resource or business rule today (grepped 2026-10-20). **The reviewer's answers at the approval, verbatim:** *"1. Agreed. 2. For now use the
same as the process owner Emily. At the moment that is a combined role. but in the future probably separated. During testing this can be set to Janine. 3. Make
payment date required when final payment is set. The the flow can set the payment status to issued. APPROVED"*
**(j) Added by amendment b, 2026-10-20:** the grant's status column is `rev_grant.rev_status` (the option set is named `rev_grantstatus`), `IsSecured=0`, values 1 Awarded, 2 Acceptance Issued, 3 Acceptance Signed, 4 Paid; the only trigger on `rev_grant` is Create Envelope's `message: 1`; `Completion` writes 3 behind a guard that the status is still 2, and `Reminders & Escalation` selects status 2 (all read from `Workflows/`, 2026-10-20). **The reviewer, verbatim:** *"Obviously the final payment should change the grant status as well."* and, on OQ-059, *"No. payment final means final."*
**(k) Added by amendment c, 2026-10-20:** build 20261020-4 was blocked. The `NoTriggerLoop` check (`src/tests/narrative/test_solution_flows.py`) rejects this flow because it triggers on `rev_payment` with `rev_paymentstatus` in the filter and writes `rev_paymentstatus` = Issued; the check ignores trigger conditions and has no guarded-self-edge mechanism, and the same shape is what the Solution Checker's `flow-avoid-recursive-loop` looks for. The reviewer, offered options, chose, verbatim: *"4"* (replace the flow's Issued write and the form-scope required rule with one table-scope rule, item 8). Microsoft Learn (`data-platform-create-business-rule`, read 2026-10-20): Entity scope is "model-driven app forms and server"; set column value and show error message are available at table scope; set requirement level is form-only; server-side rules are synchronous plug-ins whose errors reach API callers. Read from source the same day: `rev_paymentstatus`, `rev_isfinalpayment` and `rev_paymentdate` carry identical `REV_FinanceOnly` permissions (Allowed), the profile's members are the Finance team and `REV Service Accounts` only, and no other flow writes `rev_payment`.

**Decision.**

1. **Trigger.** Dataverse row trigger on `rev_payment`, `message: 4`, `scope: 4`, `runas: 3`, `filteringattributes`
   `rev_isfinalpayment,rev_paymentdate,rev_paymentstatus,rev_grantid`, outputs secured, concurrency 1. Delete is not a trigger: Finance cannot delete a
   Payment and a retention cascade deletes the Grant with it. A payment *moved* to another grant is not handled either (`A-R101`).
2. **Recompute, never react.** The trigger body supplies the payment's id and the grant id; everything else is read again: the saved payment as it is now
   (final mark, date, status, grant), the grant (its date, its own status `rev_status` and its application), the application's status, and the latest **dated** final payment on the grant (final,
   not Cancelled, date present, newest date first, one row). Target date: that payment's date; none when the read is empty. Both day values pass through
   `coalesce()` before `formatDateTime()` and `greater()`, which throw on null. **A final payment with no date is not a final and starts no clock (answer 3).**
   The form makes the date required once Final is set (§5.11), so an undated final payment can only come from a write that bypasses the form; the flow then
   reports "final payment has no date" and does not guess a day. *Previously read (rev 28 as presented, withdrawn at the approval): an undated final payment counted
   from the day its row was created (UTC), read by a second connector query for the latest undated final payment, because FR-109 needs a day that does not move on a
   later save. The reviewer's answer removes the case it handled; that query is gone. The reviewer decision it carried, OQ-057 "Payment date", is **kept**: the
   date is the payment's own, now with no exception.*
3. **One grant write: the date and the grant's own status together (amendment b, FR-113).** `UpdateOnlyRecord` on `rev_grant`, flat `item/rev_finalpaymentdate` set to the target date or
   to null, and flat `item/rev_status` set to the target status, **only when either differs from the grant's current value.** Target status: Acceptance Signed (3) to Paid (4) when a dated
   final payment exists; Paid (4) back to Acceptance Signed (3) when none does; any other status is left as it is and, when the date is written in that run, reported (FR-111, OQ-060).
   **The flow never changes a grant to 1 or 2:** the only value it ever writes that differs from the one read is 4 or 3; a grant read at 1 or 2 is written back at 1 or 2 when the date alone changes (an echo, and `A-R103`'s race). It depends on the grant's status only, never on the application's. *Previously read: "The flow never writes 1 or 2."* Setting and clearing are one action (FR-107, FR-110, FR-113).
   *Previously read (rev 28 as approved): the write carried the date only; the grant's status was excluded (item 9).*
4. **One application write.** `UpdateOnlyRecord` on `rev_application`, flat `item/rev_status`: Approved (7) to Grant Paid (11) when a final payment exists;
   Grant Paid (11) to Approved (7) when none does; any other combination writes nothing. The flow never writes any other status (FR-108, FR-110).
5. **One report.** A reason is set in four cases: a final payment with no grant, a date written while the application is at neither Approved nor Grant
   Paid, or while the grant is at Awarded or Acceptance Issued (and the mirror on clearing; the reason names which status), a saved payment that is final, not Cancelled and has no date, and a saved payment that is final and Cancelled (FR-112, as the plan words it; informational). At the end, if a reason is set, one Teams message goes to `rev_FinanceAlertUpn` and `REV | Ops | Failure Alert` is called at severity Warning.
   It carries references and the reason, never an amount, bank detail, date or name. A platform failure takes the failure path (FR-111). **Recipient (answer 2):**
   `rev_FinanceAlertUpn` is **kept as its own variable**, not folded into `rev_ProcessOwnerUpn`. Its value is the process owner for now (a combined role today, likely
   separated later) and Janine in the test environments (DEV and TST/ACC; DEV is inferred, because testing happens there). Entered as a placeholder per environment next to
   `rev_ProcessOwnerUpn` in the `pac-import-*.json` and DEV settings files, never as a literal address in a document or a flow (`no-hardcoded-environment-values`). When
   the roles split, only the value changes. While one person holds both, they get two messages for one cause.
6. **Identity and wiring.** Flow owner (`runas: 3`), because Finance cannot write Grant or Application. Existing `rev_SharedDataverse` and `rev_SharedTeams`.
   No new privilege, role, profile permission, profile member or connection reference: the earlier claim was re-checked against the profile source when answer 3 added a
   write to a secured finance column, and holds for what the flow still does; amendment c removed that write from the flow (§5.11). One new environment variable, `rev_FinanceAlertUpn`, `isrequired=1`, no default. One new workflow component: the
   table-scope business rule of items 7 and 8.
7. **The saved payment is marked Issued by the payment rule, not by the flow (answer 3; amendment c).** Branch b of item 8: Final = Yes and Payment Status = Pending sets Payment Status = Issued, in the same save. **The flow writes nothing to `rev_payment`**, so it has no edge onto its own trigger and starts no second run; it never needs to know whether the payment is Issued, because its target depends on Final, date and not-Cancelled only (§5.11). Nothing writes Pending, Cleared or Cancelled. Unticking Final, cancelling and correcting the date reverse or re-record the grant and the application and **do not revert the payment's status**. *Previously read (rev 28): one more flow write, `UpdateOnlyRecord` on `rev_payment`, `item/rev_paymentstatus` = Issued (2), last in the run and guarded by Pending, justified by a fixed-point argument and one extra no-op run (`A-CP-8`). Withdrawn: the loop check rejects it, and the reviewer chose the rule.*
8. **One table-scope business rule on `rev_payment`: the date required, and the Issued mark (answer 3; amendment c).** Scope Entity. Branch a: Final = Yes and Payment Date empty shows an error, which refuses the save on the form and on every API or import write. Branch b: not a, Final = Yes and Payment Status = Pending sets Payment Status = Issued. It never matches Cancelled, Issued or Cleared. Authored in the DEV maker designer and exported, never hand-written XAML; the exported file is checked in source and, **by amendment d (2026-10-20), edited by hand only as a "small edit" (below)**. Not a column requirement, no plug-in, and **no separate form-scope rule** (the Entity rule covers the form). It closes `A-R102` by design, pending `A-CP-9`; the flow's "final payment has no date" report stays as a backstop for rows that pre-date the rule. *Previously read (rev 28): a form-scope rule only; "API writes are caught by the flow, not blocked."*

   **Amendment d, 2026-10-20: small edits to the exported rule are allowed.** The reviewer, verbatim, answering lead-agent's proposal: *"Amend-ADR-081: Yes, that is allowed."* *Previously read (amendment c): "authored in the DEV maker designer and exported, never written as workflow XAML by hand ... the exported file is checked in source and not edited."* Now: a NEW rule is still authored once in the DEV maker designer and exported (the hand-written-XAML ban stands for new rules); after that the system MAY make a small edit directly to the exported `.xaml` (and its `.xaml.data.xml` where the edit touches it).
   - **A small edit** changes the content of one existing rule and nothing else, and is exactly one or more of: (i) the text of an error message; (ii) an option value or literal compared or set (e.g. an option number, a string); (iii) adding, removing or changing one comparison inside an existing condition (e.g. a Cancelled exclusion on branch a or b). Rule id, name, entity, scope, category, activation state, form id and the root-component registration in `Solution.xml` do not change.
   - **A new rule** is anything else, and must go back through the DEV designer: a new or removed branch or action; an action of a different kind (set column, show error, set requirement level, lock/default); a different column written or read-to-write; a change of scope or entity; a second rule on any table; a new rule file. Doubt means new rule. A rule that would need more than one condition changed to express one decision is also new.
   - **A small edit counts as done only when** (1) it is imported into DEV (`pac solution import` of the edited source, or the equivalent import the build performs) without error and the rule reads Active there; **and** (2) the `A-CP-9` checks the edit can affect are run in DEV and pass, each recorded with the date, the user it ran as and the observed result. Which checks: error text, check 1 or 2 (the message shown or returned); an option value or the Issued set, checks 1 to 3 and 5; a condition change, every check that exercises the changed branch, plus check 6 for any status the edit adds or removes from a branch. Checks 1 to 6 whole is always acceptable. Verification level is V3 at most for the edit (DEV only); TST/ACC after the managed import stays `A-CP-9`'s per-environment check.
   - **Not evidence:** a source-shape test alone (`SourceOfRule`), a clean build, or a successful import without the A-CP-9 run. An edit that imports but fails a check is not done; it is reverted in source or corrected, and reported. A rule file that was edited and not imported remains V1.
   - The `SourceOfRule` tests are updated in the same change as the edit so they assert the edited shape (no silent drift), and the Dev Summary lists each small edit: what, why, the A-CP-9 evidence. No component, column, privilege or connector is added. A reviewer decision is not needed for a small edit; it is needed for a new rule's behaviour, as ever.
   - **As-authored rule accepted with its differences** (reviewer, 2026-10-20, per Dev Summary "Revision: the payment rule is in source"): rule `Rev-Payment-Issued` (`02ac658e-9bcc-f111-a05c-7ced8d43e1b4`) is accepted as authored. (1) Branch b is an independent condition, not an else-if: a Final = Yes, undated, Pending row satisfies both, the form shows the error and also turns the status to Issued, the error stops the save, so nothing is stored; the server-side result is the design's. (2) The error text is the platform's, *"A payment date is required to set the value of "Final Payment" to Yes."*, not the designed *"A payment date is required when the payment is marked final."* (3) Default name `Rev-Payment-Issued` and description *"Click to add description"*. Any of these may later be changed as a small edit. Verification of the rule stays V1 until `A-CP-9` is run.
9. **Excluded, and why it is stated.** The pre-issue duplicate re-check (`wbs:8.5`, FR-023, `CO-010`). The Anonymised Statistic amount (§5.13 item 2). Each is
   flagged for the reviewer; none is added. **The Grant's own status "Paid" (value 4) is no longer excluded:** the reviewer put it in scope on 2026-10-20 (item 3). *Previously read
   (rev 28 as approved): excluded, because FR-107 to FR-111 did not ask for it, so a paid grant's own status would still read "Acceptance Signed".*
10. **The paid-grants retention job is not part of `wbs:8.6`** and is flagged (§5.11). It is a different artefact (a bulk-delete job over `rev_grant`,
   applied by a tenant administrator) and is not in `CO-010`. **Rev 31 note:** designed in `ADR-083` item 1 under
   `wbs:0.7` (it is a bulk-delete job over `rev_application`, joined to `rev_grant` for the date). This flow makes its
   precondition true: it sets Grant Paid and `rev_finalpaymentdate`, which are the job's two criteria.

**Consequences, in the order of the Decision.** What finance and the process owner see.

1. Finance saves a payment with Final ticked, or a final payment's date, status or grant changes: the flow starts within the platform's normal delay (not
   measured here). A save that changes none of the four columns starts nothing; the restart route is untick, save, tick, save (§5.11). *Negative:* a payment
   deleted by an administrator leaves the grant as it was.
2. **A default traced to what is seen (OQ-057, answer 3).** There is no default day any more. In the form, ticking Final makes Payment Date required, so finance cannot
   save a final payment without one; the grant's date is that date, and a later of two wins. Written by something other than the form, an undated final payment gives the
   grant **no** date and finance and the process owner see "final payment has no date". **OQ-058:** a Pending payment with Final ticked starts the clock and a Cancelled
   one never counts. *Previously read (rev 28 as presented): an undated final payment gave the grant the creation day of the payment row, in UTC.* **Amended by c:** the date is required by the table rule, so a final payment cannot be saved without one on the form or by API; only a row that pre-dates the rule, or any write if the rule fails, can lack it (`A-R102`).
3. The grant shows the date; unticking the only final payment empties it. *Negative:* a **hand-set date with no final payment behind it is cleared by the next
   save of any payment on that grant** (`A-R100`). FR-109 is read as *over a grant that already matches its payments*, because the trigger carries the new
   state and never the old, so the flow cannot tell "this save removed the mark" from "this save added an instalment". Put to the reviewer.
4. The application reads "Grant Paid"; unticking returns it to "Approved". An application at any other status (Withdrawn, say) keeps its status and the
   date is still recorded (US-026 AC-10).
   **Item 7 trace (amended by c):** a final, dated, Pending payment reads Issued in the save itself (on the form, as soon as Final is ticked), and its `modifiedby` is the finance user who saved it. *Negative:* a payment scheduled for a later day and marked final reads Issued at once; the flow cannot tell scheduled from sent. Unticking Final leaves the
   payment Issued; finance sets it back if the money did not go. Un-cancelling a final, dated payment to Pending makes it Issued.
   **Item 3 trace (grant status):** with a dated final payment saved, the grant reads Paid in the same instant the date appears; unticking the only final returns it to Acceptance Signed along with the empty date. A grant still at Awarded or Acceptance Issued keeps its status and finance and the process owner are told which; nothing moves it later by itself when the acceptance is signed (`A-R103`). A Paid grant is out of the reminder and escalation query and cannot be pulled back by `Completion`, whose guard needs status 2.
   **Item 8 trace (amended by c):** finance ticks Final with no date and the save is refused, with the error beside the date field on the form and as an error on an API or import write. *Negative:* a Final, Cancelled, undated payment cannot be saved until it is dated or Final is unticked; a row that pre-dates the rule is refused at its next save. If the rule is inactive or fails to import active, none of this holds and the flow's report is the only prompt (`A-R102`, `A-R104`).
5. Finance and the process owner receive the message. **Unset or blank `rev_FinanceAlertUpn`:** the import is refused where the Pipelines pane validates
   required variables; if a blank is entered, the Teams post fails, the writes have already been made, the run takes the failure path, the process owner is
   alerted, and **finance is told nothing**. That is a blackout for finance, written down as one, not a safe default. In PRD today the one person is both recipients.
6. No new access for anyone. The grant and application writes are attributed to the service account in audit; the payment's own status and `modifiedby` are the finance user's (amendment c).
7. The statistic's amount is unchanged. *Negative:* a reader may expect it to follow the final payment. *Previously read (rev 28 as approved): "a paid grant's own status is unchanged"; retired by item 3, since the grant now reads Paid.*
8. No record is deleted by the flow. Over-retention is not possible for years, but only if the job is built before then.

**What it reverses, and what it keeps (`IMP-1125`).** **Amendment c supersedes items 6 to 8 in part and lists every reviewer decision those items quoted, each marked.** (1) Answer 3, *"Make payment date required when final payment is set"*: **kept, and stronger** (refused server-side as well as on the form). (2) Answer 3, *"Then the flow can set the payment status to issued"*: **kept in outcome, reversed in mechanism**: the payment becomes Issued, set by the rule and not by the flow, which is the reviewer's own decision *"4"*, not a reading of ours. (3) OQ-059, *"No. payment final means final."*: **kept**; unticking leaves the payment Issued. (4) OQ-057 *"Payment date"*, OQ-058, answer 1 on `A-R100` and answer 2 on `rev_FinanceAlertUpn`: **kept**. Nothing else is reversed. The reviewer's 2026-09-09 *"decide later"* (rev 6) is resolved by his 2026-10-20
decision above; the rev 6 wording is kept as history in §3.5, §5.11 and `A-R56`. Kept: ADR-048 (finance is an area in the Grant Administration app), ADR-045,
NFR-150 (no rollup or copy of a secured value; this flow copies none), and `CO-010`'s limit that the high end of its hours rises if a retry or a missing-grant
case needs more than a logged alert. **This design stops at the alert.** What may raise the high end: the new environment variable and one Teams post, which
`commercial-agent` should confirm are inside "a logged alert".

**Rejected options.** *React to the change* (set the date when the final mark is ticked, clear it when removed): needs the old value, which the trigger does not
carry, and gives repeat saves, corrections and cancellations three code paths. *Run as the modifying user:* Finance cannot write Grant or Application. *A
column on Payment to show the reason to finance:* a new secured column, an import prerequisite (`C-TECH-050`) and more than `CO-010`'s two writes. *Tell finance
through the Error Log only:* Finance has no privilege on it. *Fall back to the day the flow runs, or the day the row was created, for an undated payment:* the first moves the date on every later save and breaks FR-109; the
second was the design as presented and is withdrawn by answer 3. *Make `rev_paymentdate` required on the column:* unconditional, blocks Pending payments with no date, and is
not enforced for API writes. *A plug-in to refuse an undated final payment:* a new component class outside `CO-010`. *Revert Issued to Pending when Final is unticked:* the flow
cannot see whether the money went out. *Skip the extra run with a trigger condition on Issued:* un-cancelling straight to Issued needs the recompute. *Add the paid-grants job or the duplicate re-check here:* not in `CO-010`. **Amendment c:** *Keep the Issued write and add a guarded-self-edge mechanism to the loop check:* a new mechanism in a check the flow was not the reason for, to keep a write the platform can do without; the reviewer chose the rule. *A trigger condition that skips Issued:* still rejected (un-cancelling straight to Issued needs the recompute), and the checker ignores conditions anyway. *Keep a form-scope required rule beside the flow's Issued write:* the rev 28 design. *Exclude Cancelled from branch a:* not taken; offered as a one-line alternative in §5.11.

**Flow size.** About **28 actions** in one scope after amendment c (§5.11's count; this figure predated amendment b's additions and is two fewer than they make it, the Issued guard and its write being gone) (four reads, two writes, the reasons built as one `Compose` of conditional fragments, one report block, the failure path). *As built, counted from the shipped JSON 2026-10-20: 27 actions plus the trigger; the Dev Summary's "about 40" is not what the file holds.*
**Judgement:** proportionate for two writes and their reversal; nothing is nested deeper than four levels.

### ADR-082: Automation #5 cost and size — one extractor call per batch of columns, one prompt that rewrites and corrects spelling, and the action ceiling raised to 125

**Status:** `Accepted` (rev 30, approved 2026-10-21 by Xander Lykopoulos, verbatim *"Approved"*, relayed by lead-agent). The reviewer's three decisions D1 to D3 of 2026-10-21 are recorded and applied. · **Date:** 2026-10-21 · **WBS:** `wbs:5.3` (the flow), `wbs:5.6` (spelling, under `CO-009`, approved unbilled) · **Amends** `ADR-075` item 1 (the extractor call), item 2 (the offsets it reads), item 4 (the spelling call), item 6 (check P2), its Rejected option *"One prompt for rewrite and spelling"*, and its flow-size paragraph; see the note under `ADR-075`'s status line. **Open item, not designed here:** `IMP-1190` (below).

**Context.** The reviewer's decisions, relayed by lead-agent on 2026-10-21 (his wording is not in the hand-off, so no quotation marks):
**D1** one extractor call per application, columns joined with a fixed separator and mapped back by offset, split into the fewest batches under the per-call limit, a failed call marking every column in its batch `ai-error`;
**D2** the spelling prompt merged into the rewrite prompt, the TAD to say what replaces the word-by-word guard;
**D3** the 100-action ceiling lifted, the TAD to set a new one it can justify.

| Fact | Level |
|---|---|
| The extractor is billed **20 credits per started 1,000 characters, per call**. DEV's two measured days: 460 of 626 credits went to extraction; one 3,000 to 4,000 character column cost 80; the rewrite prompt costs 4 (one reading 7) and the spelling prompt 3 (one reading 6) per column. The flow calls the extractor once per column, about 5 columns per application, about 1,200 characters in all, so most columns pay a whole 1,000-character block for a few hundred characters | E1 (`IMP-1189`: the consumption report reconciles with `msdyn_aievent.msdyn_creditconsumed`, DEV, 2026-10-19 and 2026-10-20; lead-agent) |
| The published rate: *advanced text analysis, entity extraction*, 20 AI Builder credits per 1,000 characters | E2 (Microsoft Learn, *Overview of licensing*, AI Builder capability rate table, read 2026-10-21) |
| **The per-call text limit of the prebuilt entity extraction model is 5,000 characters**: *"Documents can't exceed 5,000 characters."* The flow already used this figure as a per-column cap (`ADR-075` item 1) without a cited source | E2 (Microsoft Learn, *Entity extraction prebuilt model*, "Supported data format and languages", read 2026-10-21) |
| A cloud flow definition holds **500 actions**, nests **8 levels**, and an expression holds **8,192 characters**; Microsoft adds that a flow with many actions may edit slowly even under 500. The project's "100" was therefore never a platform limit | E2 (Microsoft Learn, *Limits of automated, scheduled, and instant flows*, "Flow definition limits", read 2026-10-21) |
| The flow has 100 actions and 5 levels of nesting (the definition test's own count); the extractor and its answer are two of them, inside the per-column loop | E1 (counted from source, 2026-10-21) |
| `take`, `join`, `range`, `skip`, `union`, `decodeUriComponent` and `first` are already used in the scrub flow (7, 23, 11, 128, 15, 73 hits); no other function is introduced | E1 (`grep -o -F` over the flow JSON, 2026-10-21) |

**Decision.** Eight interventions, traced in the same order under Consequences.

1. **One extractor call per batch, and a batch is as many columns as fit.** The columns chosen by `Filter_columns_to_scrub` are taken in their fixed order. A column joins the open batch when the batch's length plus the separator plus the column's length is at most **5,000 characters**; otherwise it opens the next batch (*next fit*: order kept, no column split, no look-back). The per-column cap of 5,000 (`ADR-075` item 1) stays, so a column always fits a batch alone. The separator is **two line feeds** (2 characters). The text sent is each column's raw text **exactly as stored, not trimmed**, joined by the separator, so the batch length that counts against the limit, and the characters billed, include the separators. Both numbers are constants in `Compose_constants` (a platform limit and a format; `IMP-1076` inventory below), not settings. *Typical case:* 5 columns, about 1,200 characters, **one call**. Implementation shape: a variable `batchPlan` (an array of objects `{raw, red, batch, used}` holding **logical column names and numbers only**, never text), initialised at the top of the flow with the other variables (check 4), filled by a sequential loop over `Filter_columns_to_scrub` in which one `Compose` reads the last element of the plan (`first(skip(…))`, the existing precedent) and one `AppendToArrayVariable` adds the next. An outer `Foreach` over `range(0, number of batches)` (empty when no column is chosen) runs, per batch: filter the plan to the batch, select its column texts, compose the joined text, select each column's layout, call the extractor once, and run the existing per-column loop over the batch's layout. **Fewest batches** means fewest for this order-preserving rule. A true minimum is a bin-packing problem a flow cannot solve; next fit is within a factor of two of it, equals it whenever the whole application fits one batch, and a worse split costs only credits, never correctness.
2. **Each entity goes back to its column by offset, and anything that straddles a boundary fails closed.** `Select_batch_layout` gives each column in the batch its `start` (0 for the first, otherwise `length(join(take(texts, i), separator)) + length(separator)`) and its `end` (`start + length`). For a column, `Filter_column_entities` keeps the entities that **touch** it (`startIndex < end` and `startIndex + length > start`), and `Select_column_entities` rebases each kept entity to the column (`startIndex − start`) and sets `crosses` when it is not wholly inside (`startIndex < start` or `startIndex + length > end`). Rebased entities have the shape the per-column actions already read (`type`, `value`, `startIndex`, `length`, `score`), so the labelling, the name trim and widening, the practice walk, P1 and P3 are unchanged, and each runs against its own column's raw text. **An entity with `crosses` is treated exactly as a partial overlap of two spans is today:** `overlapping-identifiers:<column>`, that column **not written**, for every column the entity touches. An entity wholly inside the separator touches no column and is dropped. The offset clamp of `ADR-075` item 2 moves into `Select_column_entities`. *Property:* every character the extractor labelled is labelled in exactly one column or holds every column it touches.
3. **A failed batch marks every column in it `ai-error`.** `Compose_batch_entities` is null after a failed, timed-out or unreadable call (`A-NS-34`, unchanged). Each column of that batch then reaches the existing `else` branch (`Append_reason_ai_error`) and nothing is sent to the prompt for it. Columns in other batches are unaffected. The retry policy of the call is unchanged.
4. **One prompt rewrites and corrects spelling.** `Run_the_spelling_prompt`, `Compose_spelling` and `Select_spelling_words` are removed from the flow. `REV Narrative Rewrite Prompt` takes over the correction. It keeps its five inputs (`Narrative`, `NeutralTerms`, `Titles`, `NameRules`, `Labels`) and gains **no input**: the spelling rule is part of the fixed template (`ADR-076` item 4), not a tunable list. Spelling is corrected **before** the rules are applied, so a misspelt key word (*husbnd*) is still neutralised. The component `REV Narrative Spelling Prompt` is no longer called.
5. **The merged prompt's output contract** (the flow depends on it; Emily does not change it). Plain text, in this order:
   (a) the rewritten, spelling-corrected text, and nothing else; then
   (b) only if at least one word was corrected: a line holding exactly `###CORRECTIONS###`, then one line per correction in the form `wrong=>right`, the misspelt word as it stands in the text, and the word that replaced it, each a single word, no spaces.
   The flow splits the answer at the **first** `###CORRECTIONS###`: the text before it (trailing white space removed) is the rewrite; each line after it is a *declared correction*. No such line means no corrections, and the whole answer is the rewrite. A line that is not of the form `word=>word` is ignored. `finishReason` must be `stop` (`A-NS-8`), as now. Model `gpt-41-mini`, temperature 0, moderation Low, output `text`, unchanged. *The template's wording of the new paragraphs is a proposal for the reviewer to apply in DEV (R1d, §12.6.1); the contract above, not the wording, is what the flow reads:*
   > *Spelling.* Before applying any rule, correct each word of the text that is misspelt or mistyped. Correct a word only if it starts with a lower-case letter and the correct word starts with the same letter and has the same number of letters give or take two. Never change a word that starts with a capital letter, a label in square brackets, a number, a name of a condition, a medicine or a treatment. Then apply the lists below to the corrected text.
   > *Reply.* Reply with the rewritten text only. If you corrected any word, add a line `###CORRECTIONS###`, and under it one line per corrected word, `misspelt=>corrected`, in lower case, nothing else.
   And the existing closing paragraph's *"do not correct spelling"* and *"Use only words that are in the text or in the lists above"* are reworded to *"apart from the spelling corrections you list"*.
6. **Check P2 tolerates a corrected spelling only as a declared, validated near-spelling, and nothing else changes.** *The property* (the closed set of sources a written word may come from): every word of the rewrite, labels removed, is **(i)** a word of the labelled input, **(ii)** a word of the closed list, **(iii)** a plural form of an input word, as now, or **(iv) the corrected half of a declared correction that passes the pair rule**. A word from none of the four gives `rewrite-invalid:<column>` and the column **is not written**. *The pair rule, one way of meeting the property* (item 4 of `ADR-075`, moved from *position* to *pair*): a declared `wrong=>right` is valid when **all** hold: `wrong` is a word of the labelled input as written there and **starts with a lower-case letter** (the `replace()` trick of `A-NS-35`, as `Select_spelling_words` did); `right` starts with the same letter as `wrong`; their lengths differ by at most 2; both are letters, with an optional internal hyphen or apostrophe, and neither contains `[` or `]`; `wrong` is not a closed-list word; and `right` is not a gendered word (`RedactionNeutralTerms`' left side, as P3). One `Select` (`Select_valid_corrections`) turns the declared lines into the pipe-delimited list of valid `right` words, which `Compose_check_texts` carries beside `inputPipe`, and `Filter_added_words` gains one `contains()` against it. **Why this cannot let an added word through:** a word outside (i) to (iii) is accepted only as a near-spelling of a lower-case word that is already in the text, so what it adds is at most a two-letter change to an existing word. Names, streets, numbers and anything capitalised are labelled before the model sees the text or start with a capital, and so cannot be the corrected half of a valid pair. A word the model changes **without** declaring it, or changes beyond the pair rule, fails (i) to (iv). **Lost, stated plainly:** the old rule proved *where* a corrected word sat (same position, same word count); the pair rule cannot, because a rewrite changes word counts. A valid corrected word may therefore appear anywhere, and more than once. P1 and P3 still run on the final text, which is now the rewrite itself (`Compose_final_text` becomes a one-line alias for it, or goes). The fidelity checks are unchanged.
7. **Retired.** `ADR-075` item 4 (the separate spelling call and its word-by-word acceptance) and its oracle `accept_spelling`; `A-NS-35`'s use for the position test (it is still used for the pair rule's lower-case test). The per-column extraction actions are renamed and moved, not duplicated.
8. **The action ceiling is 125, and nesting stays at most 6.** The flow is about **109 actions** after this ADR (table below), 6 levels deep (one more than today: the batch loop wraps the column loop; the platform allows 8). The definition test's 100 becomes **125** and its nesting limit 5 becomes **6**. *Why 125:* the platform limit (500) does not bind and is not the measure; the reviewer rejected 340 for this job as absurd and accepted about 100, so the ceiling sits a quarter above the size he last accepted, which leaves room for this ADR and one small later change, not for a new stage. It is a ceiling, not a budget: a change that would cross it goes back to the reviewer with what it proposes to remove. *Maintainability judgement:* the flow is still read as six parts (below); the nested batch loop is the one new thing a maker must understand, and it is a single sentence (*"group the columns into calls of at most 5,000 characters, then do per column what was done before"*). It does not add a stage to the checks.

**The flow a maker reads — about 109 actions (100 before).**

| Change | Actions |
|---|---|
| Before | 100 |
| `Initialise_batch_plan` (top level, with the other three variables) | +1 |
| The plan loop: `For_each_plan_column`, `Compose_batch_step`, `Append_batch_plan` | +3 |
| The batch loop and its set-up: `For_each_batch`, `Filter_batch_columns`, `Select_batch_texts`, `Compose_batch_joined`, `Select_batch_layout` | +5 |
| `Extract_entities_from_the_column` and `Compose_entities` move up a level and become `Extract_entities_from_the_batch` and `Compose_batch_entities` | 0 |
| Per column: `Filter_column_entities`, `Select_column_entities` | +2 |
| Spelling: `Run_the_spelling_prompt`, `Compose_spelling`, `Select_spelling_words` removed; `Select_valid_corrections` added | −2 |
| **After** | **about 109** |

Every new action that carries narrative text (`Select_batch_texts`, `Compose_batch_joined`, `Select_batch_layout`, the extractor call, `Compose_batch_entities`, `Filter_column_entities`, `Select_column_entities`, `Select_valid_corrections`) has `secureData` on inputs, and on outputs where it is not a `Compose` (a `Compose` secures `inputs` only, check 18). The plan variable holds names and numbers, so "no variable holds text" still stands.

**Not decided here: `IMP-1190`, an open item.** `msdyn_aievent.msdyn_datainfo` keeps the input text of every AI Builder call (measured in DEV, `IMP-1190`), including the raw, unscrubbed columns sent to the extractor and the labelled text and rule rows sent to the prompt; `secureData` hides run history only. §5.5's paragraph *"What is never in run history, a log or a notification"* and the statement that the raw narrative is read by the flow and the Admin role only are therefore **not true of this Dataverse table**, and DPIA and RoPA entries that rest on them are in question. This ADR neither fixes nor worsens it: the joined call stores the same text once, in one row, where five calls stored it in five. Retention, who can read `msdyn_aievent`, and a PRD bulk-delete are for a later decision, tracked as `A-R105` and `A-NS-45`. **Rev 31:** decided by the reviewer (D-1, 2026-10-22) and designed in `ADR-083`; the heading's *"Not decided here"* stays true of this ADR.

**Rejected.**

- **Keep two prompts and tolerate a corrected spelling in P2 by a count** (*up to N unexplained words per column*). It lets an added word through whenever it is among the N, and it keeps the second call's 3 credits per column, which D2 removes.
- **JSON output from the prompt** (`{"text": …, "corrections": […]}`). Cleaner to parse, but a structured-output path through `responsev2.predictionOutput` has never been run in this solution; it would be a new platform contract on a flow that has none open. The delimiter keeps the existing `predictionOutput.text` path (`A-NS-8`, `A-NS-33`). Revisit when the structured path has been exercised elsewhere.
- **The model rewrites and corrects, and P2 simply allows any near-spelling of any input word.** Needs "exists an input word such that …" for every output word: a nested loop over words that a flow expression cannot write. Declaring the pair makes the check linear.
- **Closed-form batching** (batch number from the column's start offset divided by 5,000, a straddling column alone). No loop, about 6 fewer actions, but a rule a maker cannot state in one sentence and up to twice the calls of next fit on a long application. Rejected for readability; it is the fallback if the plan loop proves heavier than it looks.
- **Keeping the extraction per column.** Rejected by D1: about three quarters of the flow's credits.
- **One variable holding the batch's entities, so the column loop need not nest.** It would hold entity `value`s, which are narrative text; "no variable holds text" (`ADR-075`, flow notes) is kept.
- **Call the extractor once for the whole application, whatever the length.** Over 5,000 characters the service refuses the call (E2); D1 asks for the fewest batches under the limit.

**Reviewer decisions quoted in `ADR-075`, each kept or reversed.**

| Decision (as `ADR-075` quotes it) | Here |
|---|---|
| *"Yes, the AI prompt processed in EU is agreed."* (2026-10-16) | Kept. The merged prompt is the same component, same model and region |
| Flex routing disabled at tenant level (2026-10-16) | Kept |
| Spelling "as a second call … I think it's better to keep it separated. This feature should be added to the design" (2026-10-16) | **Reversed in part, by D2 (2026-10-21):** the spelling correction is kept; keeping it a **separate** call is reversed. `ADR-075`'s *Rejected: One prompt for rewrite and spelling. The reviewer prefers two* no longer stands |
| `CO-009` approved, unbilled | Kept. No change-order trigger: no new requirement, a smaller flow in credits |
| *"Simplify the workflow, 340 actions is absurd…"* (2026-10-16) | Kept. The flow stays near 100. The figure *"100 is the ceiling"* was this document's own, not his; D3 raises it |
| *"Approved Design revision 22"*, *"Approved for revision 23"*, Iteration 11 *"Yes please, process the suggested changes"*, *"1. Approved"* (rev 25), *"LAbel the name and approved for development"* (rev 29), the `husband` ruling, *"All fields in the trustee portal right now…"* | Kept. Trim and widening, the practice walk, P1 and P3 run per column on its own raw text and rebased offsets |

**Consequences**, in the order of the Decision:

1. *User sees:* nothing different for an ordinary application: one extractor call where there were about five. *Cost:* per application the extractor falls from about 100 credits to about 33 (the reviewer's estimate, `IMP-1189`; the exact figure is 20 × the started 1,000 characters of the joined text, separators included, `A-NS-44`). An application over 5,000 characters in all pays one call per batch, as it paid one per column before. *Negative:* a batch is one call, so one failure takes every column in it (intervention 3).
2. *User sees:* a column held with `overlapping-identifiers:<column>` when a found value straddles two columns' text. *Negative:* the extractor now reads several answers as one document; a value that runs across the separator is held rather than split. *Open:* how often that happens in real answers is unmeasured (`A-NS-41`, the first DEV sweep); the held column goes to the process owner, who reviews every record anyway (`ADR-078`).
3. *User sees:* `ai-error:<column>` on every column of the application when the one call fails, where one failure used to hit one column. The record is in the review list with the card either way.
4. *User sees:* corrected spelling, as before. *Credits:* the spelling call's 3 per column goes; the rewrite call gains a few lines of template and a few output lines, small against it. *Negative:* the model now decides in one pass, so a spelling it gets wrong in a way the pair rule refuses (a longer change, a capitalised word, a word it did not declare) **stops that column from being written**, where in two calls the slip was left as written and nothing stopped. That is the price of D2, and its size is unmeasured: the `wbs:5.7` scoring run counts `rewrite-invalid` attributable to an undeclared or refused correction, and a rate that is too high comes back to the reviewer as a choice between loosening the pair rule and returning to two calls.
5. *User sees:* nothing, unless the model does not follow the output form: a missing delimiter means "no corrections", a malformed correction line is ignored, and a corrected word that was not declared is `rewrite-invalid`. *What a person sees by default:* with the **old** prompt still in DEV (R1d not done) the answer carries no corrections and no delimiter, so the new flow writes the column with no spelling correction and no blackout. With the **new** prompt and the **old** flow, every column fails P2 on the delimiter line's words: a blackout of DEV. **Order matters: deploy the flow first, edit the prompt second** (TST/ACC and PRD receive both in one solution).
6. *User sees:* `rewrite-invalid` means the model added or changed a word beyond the four sources; nothing is written; the process owner writes the counterpart. *Positive:* a prompt injection can still at most move or drop words already there, or change one by a near-spelling.
7. *User sees:* nothing. The tests that proved the second call are replaced (below).
8. *User sees:* nothing. The maker sees about 109 actions, the new part being one nested loop.

**What a person sees by default** (`IMP-0511`). No new setting, no new default. `RedactionPromptStage` = `off` is still the kill switch: with it `off` no column is written (`prompt-stage-off`), before any batch is planned. With the plan empty (every column already has a counterpart, is empty or is too long) the batch loop runs zero times and **no extractor call is made**: the batch count is `0`, not `1`, so an empty joined text is never sent.

**Lists, inventoried** (`IMP-1076`).

| List | Kind | Where |
|---|---|---|
| The 5,000-character call limit, the two-line-feed separator | A platform limit and a format specification | Constants in `Compose_constants`, changed with tests |
| The pair rule's numbers (same first letter, length within 2) | Specification of the check | Constants, changed with tests; not a setting (a looser rule weakens a safety property and is the reviewer's, not Emily's) |
| The spelling instruction in the template | Fixed contract | The component, not a setting; Emily changes no spelling rule |
| The closed list, the gendered list | Derived from `RedactionNeutralTerms`, `RedactionLabels` and the constants (`ADR-076`) | Unchanged |
| The `rev_setting` rows | None added, none retired | — |

**Functions and contracts it adds.** No new expression function (grepped, table above). New platform contracts, each an OPEN row in §12.6 with a marker at its point of use (`C-TECH-052`): `A-NS-41` (offsets over a joined text), `A-NS-42` (a nested `Foreach` that reads an action of its enclosing iteration saves), `A-NS-43` (the merged prompt's output form), `A-NS-44` (the billing of a joined call), `A-NS-45` (`msdyn_aievent` retention, `IMP-1190`). `A-NS-35` (`replace()` is case-sensitive) now also carries the pair rule's lower-case test; `A-NS-8`, `A-NS-33` and `A-NS-34` apply to the merged call as they did to the rewrite.

**What the tests must prove** (development-agent; the narrative suite, `unit-tests`). In the oracle, `plan_batches`, `map_entities` and `validate_corrections` replace `accept_spelling`, and the flow definition test and the WDL simulator (`wdl_sim.py`) learn a nested `Foreach`. *Batching:* one batch when the total is at most 5,000 including separators; a total of 5,001 gives two; a 5,000-character column alone; two 3,000-character columns give two batches; order is kept; no column chosen gives zero batches and no call. *Mapping:* an entity in the third column rebases to that column; an entity that starts in one column and ends in the next gives `overlapping-identifiers` on **both** and writes neither; an entity inside the separator is dropped; CRLF in a column does not move the next column's offsets (the property of `A-NS-41`; the live check is the DEV sweep). *Failure:* a null `Compose_batch_entities` gives `ai-error` on each of the batch's columns and none in another batch. *Merged output:* the delimiter splits at the first occurrence; no delimiter, no corrections; a malformed line is ignored. *The pair rule, the safety proof:* a rewrite that adds a name, a phone number or a sentence is held by P2 as before; a **declared** near-spelling of a lower-case input word is written; the same correction **undeclared**, declared with a different first letter, a length change of 3, a capitalised `wrong`, a `wrong` that is not in the input, or a `right` that is a gendered word, is `rewrite-invalid`; a declared pair does not excuse a *different* added word. *Size:* at most 125 actions, at most 6 levels, no `Until`, no `result()`, `secureData` on every action that sees text.

**Gate interactions** (`config/revitalise-grant-automation-build.yml`, the steps over `Workflows/`):

| Gate | Trips? |
|---|---|
| `flow-definition-language`, the checks not named in the next rows (1 to 10 live in the engine's script, 14 to 17 here) | Not expected to: no new action type, no new function, no new write shape; development-agent confirms by running the gate, since this ADR reads only the instance script's own header for checks 11 to 18 |
| `flow-definition-language` check 4 (`InitializeVariable` scoping) | **Watch.** `batchPlan` is initialised at the top level with `reasons`, `scores` and `anyScrubbed`, never inside the scope or a loop |
| `flow-definition-language` check 11 (secure outputs on a personal-data read) | No: no new read of a personal column |
| `flow-definition-language` check 12 (no reference into a loop from outside it; the designer refuses it once nesting passes one level, measured 2026-10-09) | **The new nesting is exactly its precondition.** No expression outside either loop may call `body()`, `outputs()`, `actions()` or `result()` on an action inside one: the loops hand results out only through `reasons`, `scores` and `anyScrubbed`, and the batch count and the plan are read by `variables()`. An inner action reading an action of the **enclosing** iteration is inside-out, not what check 12 forbids, and not measured: `A-NS-42` |
| `flow-definition-language` check 13 (every `Until` ends) | No: no `Until` |
| `flow-definition-language` check 18 (a `Compose` secures `inputs` only) | **Watch:** `Compose_batch_joined`, `Compose_batch_entities`, `Compose_batch_step` |
| `flow-definition-language` self-test fixtures that name the retired actions | Check them: a fixture naming `Run_the_spelling_prompt` or `Select_spelling_words` is a CHECK to correct, not a reason to keep the actions (`IMP-0692`) |
| `flow-reads-no-trigger-body` | No |
| `unit-tests` (the narrative suite) | **Yes, by design:** the size test (100 and 5 become 125 and 6), the spelling tests, `test_prompt_component.py`'s `SPELLING` entry and its `Run_the_spelling_prompt` row, the oracle |
| `source-validate`, `root-components-resolve`, `guid-syntax` | No, unless the spelling component is removed from `Other/Customizations.xml`: then the root-component list changes in the same commit. Left in the solution and uncalled it trips nothing (the rev 20 detector precedent, §5.5) |
| `assumption-register`, `assumption-markers`, `assumption-id-collisions` | **Yes, by design:** five new ids, `A-NS-41` to `A-NS-45`, each needing a marker at its point of use and a Dev Summary §10 row. Free across the TAD and both Dev Summaries (grepped 2026-10-21; the highest in use is `A-NS-40`) |
| `no-hardcoded-thresholds`, `domain-invariants`, `superseded-column-writers`, `tad-coverage`, `no-special-category-data-in-scoring`, `pack-*` | No: no new column, no new writer, no threshold the flow decides on, no new file |

**What development-agent rewrites** (retired words searched across the repository with `git grep -n -E` and a positive control, 2026-10-21; `logs/` excluded, the finding log is history):

### ADR-083: Two retention jobs join the set — paid grants after six years, and AI Builder's own copy of the narrative after 30 days in PRD

**Status:** `Accepted` (rev 31, approved 2026-10-22, verbatim *"2. Approved"*; item 2's daily cadence confirmed, verbatim *"1. Yes, daily."*) · **Date:** 2026-10-22 · **WBS:** `wbs:0.7` (Data governance & compliance: retention
policies for applicant PII; its evidence rule already names `ensure-bulk-delete-jobs.ps1`) · **Implements** reviewer
decision D-1 (2026-10-22) and R4 (*"Go ahead and build."*) · **Closes by design** `A-R105`; narrows `A-NS-45`.

**Context.** (a) The retention schedule (`knowledge/domain/regulations.md`, Retention Schedule) deletes a successful
grant's full record six years after the final payment date. `ADR-004` and NFR-010 named that job from rev 1, but the
script header deferred it *"in the release that ships"* `rev_grant`, and when `ADR-081` (rev 28) made the final payment
date real it left the job out of `wbs:8.6` on purpose. Measured 2026-10-22: `prd-settings.json` and
`test-settings.json` hold four jobs each and no paid-grant job; `dev-settings.json` holds none. So a paid grant's
record, health free text included, would be kept for ever. (b) AI Builder writes one `msdyn_aievent` row per call,
with the call's input text in `msdyn_datainfo`, measured in DEV (rev 30, `A-R105`). Microsoft Learn (*Monitor AI
Builder models and prompts activity*, updated 2026-01-14, read 2026-10-22) says the data *"persists in the table
even if you delete the model, cloud flow, and app"* and gives a recurring bulk delete with `OlderThanXDays` as the way to
remove it. It states no retention of its own, so without a job the rows stay for ever. (c) The reviewer decided both on
2026-10-22, quoted in the rev 31 entry.

**Decision.** Four interventions, traced in the same order under Consequences.

1. **Paid-grant job.** A `dataverse.bulkDeleteJobs` entry, `jobKey` `paidGrantApplications`, name
   `REV Retention - Paid Grant Applications`, entity `rev_application`, `retentionValue` 72, `retentionUnit` `months`,
   `FREQ=MONTHLY;INTERVAL=1`, `startTimeUtc` `01:40`, in `test-settings.json` and `prd-settings.json`. Its `jobKey`
   branch in `New-RetentionQuerySet` builds: `rev_application.rev_status` Equal 11 (Grant Paid), with an Inner
   `LinkEntity` from `rev_application.rev_applicationid` to `rev_grant.rev_applicationid` whose `LinkCriteria` is
   `rev_finalpaymentdate` `OlderThanXMonths` the retention value. The shape is the existing withdrawn/incomplete
   branch's (a date on a related row, tested in `LinkCriteria`), pointed the other way along the relationship. Months,
   not years: `OlderThanXMonths` is the operator the script already uses, and 72 is six years exactly. The cascade
   from Application removes Grant, Review and Payment; the orphan sweep at 02:40 then removes the Applicant and,
   by cascade, the Bank Account.
2. **AI Event job.** A `dataverse.bulkDeleteJobs` entry, `jobKey` `aiEvents`, name `REV Retention - AI Events`,
   entity `msdyn_aievent`, `retentionValue` 30, `retentionUnit` `days`, `FREQ=DAILY;INTERVAL=1`, `startTimeUtc`
   `03:30`, **in `prd-settings.json` only**. Its branch builds one condition, `createdon` `OlderThanXDays` the
   retention value, no status test (every row is a call's input). **Daily, not monthly**, so the DPIA can say *at most
   31 days*: a monthly run would let a row reach about 60. The reviewer's *"30-day"* is read as the age at which a row
   goes; if he meant a run every 30 days, only `recurrencePattern` changes.
3. **The script.** Two new `switch` branches; the header's paid-grant deferral sentence is replaced by the six-job list
   of §3.4.1; nothing else in the script changes. The existence check, `CREATED`/`EXISTS`/`FAILED` reporting and
   recurrence-drift warning already apply to every entry (C-TECH-042). `DAILY` is passed through as written.
4. **Who can read `msdyn_aievent`** (settles `A-NS-45` by design). *The property:* only identities already trusted
   with Tier 4 text can read a row, and no person reads it as part of the process. *The current way of meeting it*, on
   Microsoft Learn's role table (same page): System Administrator and System Customizer see all activity; Basic User
   and Environment Maker see only their own; a row is *"processed by"* the flow's owner. So: (a) no `REV` role carries
   any `msdyn_aievent` privilege, measured in source 2026-10-22 (none of the four `Roles/*.xml` names it), and none is
   added; (b) in TST/ACC and PRD no person in an application role holds System Administrator or System Customizer,
   which §6.5 already requires of Emily and the service account; (c) the scrub flow in TST/ACC and PRD is owned by a
   non-interactive identity (the service account or the deploy identity), so its rows are no person's *own activity*.
   **Residual, stated:** the tenant administrator can read the rows, as that role can read every secured column, so
   this adds no new reader; and the rows exist for up to 31 days instead of for ever.
   **Note, rev 33 approval (2026-10-22):** (c) was measured false as worded in DEV — the rows are owned by
   `svc_grantapplications`, a sign-in account holding System Administrator (`IMP-1219`). The reviewer accepted it,
   verbatim *"2. Accepted."*; recorded as `A-R109`.

**Also decided, not an intervention:** the DPIA and RoPA name `msdyn_aievent` as a store of special-category text
(contents, PRD location, 30-day retention, readers as item 4). They are Revitalise's documents (`docs/Import/`), not
this repository's to edit; §12 carries the update as an external item before PRD use.

**Consequences, in the order of the Decision.**

1. *User sees:* nothing in the app. A paid grant's application, review, grant, payments, applicant and bank account
   disappear on the first monthly run after six years from the final payment date. *Negative:* an application at
   Grant Paid with no grant row, or a grant with no final payment date, matches nothing and is kept. `ADR-081` makes
   both states unreachable once the flow is live; `A-R100`'s pre-PRD listing finds any made by hand. The signed PDF in
   SharePoint, the DocuSign envelope and the anonymised-statistic check are §5.12's helper flow, not this job, and are
   unchanged by this ADR. *Default traced:* if the entry is missing from a settings file, the script creates nothing
   for it and says nothing, so the record is kept for ever; the settings test (gate interactions) is what makes a
   missing entry fail a build.
2. *User sees:* the AI Builder activity page in PRD (Power Automate → Automation center) shows at most 30 days, and
   anyone reading per-call cost from `msdyn_aievent` (`knowledge/technology/power-automate.md`) must read within 30
   days. Whether Microsoft's credit reporting also loses the deleted rows is **not stated** by Microsoft: `A-NS-46`,
   OPEN. *Erasure and SAR (C-DOM-005, C-DOM-006):* §5.12's locate step does not search `msdyn_aievent`; a row is gone
   within 31 days, inside the one-month response period, so an erasure request is met by the job, and a SAR answered
   within the month must say that AI Builder held the narrative text for up to 30 days. *Default traced:* DEV and TST/ACC keep every row; that is the reviewer's decision and rests on their holding
   test text only (§3.4.1).
3. *Negative:* two more query builders in the most intricate script in `provisioning/`, each needing its own unit
   test. Neither has been run against a live environment, and nor has any existing job (no deployment record shows
   one created): `A-RET-1` and `A-NS-47`.
4. *User sees:* nothing. The design gives the table no new reader, and the verification is `A-NS-45` as rewritten.

**Rejected.** (a) *Export AI events to CSV before deleting*, as Microsoft Learn offers: it makes a further, unmanaged
copy of the special-category text the job exists to remove. (b) *A flow that deletes AI events*: `ADR-004` already
chose native bulk delete over a sweep flow, for the same reasons. (c) *The paid-grant job over `rev_grant`*: deleting
the Grant would leave the Application and its narratives behind; the schedule deletes the full record, which is the
Application.

**WBS.** Both jobs are retention policies for applicant PII, which is what `wbs:0.7` contracts, and the task's evidence
rule already names this script, so neither is a change order. Neither is `wbs:8.6` (`CO-010` excludes it) or
`wbs:5.3`. Whether the added work fits `wbs:0.7`'s estimate is commercial-agent's to judge from `contract/wbs.json`.

**Gate interactions** (the build config's `unit-tests` step runs the provisioning Pester suites; grepped
`src/tests/provisioning/` for `bulkDeleteJobs`, `ensure-bulk-delete` and `New-RetentionQuerySet`):

| Check | Trips? | What development-agent does |
|---|---|---|
| `DeploymentSettings.Tests.ps1`, *"four monthly/weekly bulk-delete jobs are declared in both environments"* | **Yes** | Rewrite: the five personal-data jobs in both TST/ACC and PRD, `aiEvents` in PRD, and `aiEvents` **absent** from `test-settings.json` (so a copy-paste cannot quietly add it) |
| same file, *"retention periods are identical in both environments"* | No | Iterates TST/ACC's jobs; `aiEvents` is PRD-only and `paidGrantApplications` is in both |
| same file, *"the error-log job is the only one measured in days, and it is 90"* | Title only | The assertion holds; rename it, and add `aiEvents` = 30 days in PRD |
| `DataverseScripts.Tests.ps1`, *"creates all four jobs…"* and the recurrence regex `^FREQ=(MONTHLY\|WEEKLY);INTERVAL=1$` | **Yes**, once the fixture carries the new jobs | Count from the fixture; admit `DAILY` |
| `DataverseScripts.Tests.ps1`, unknown `jobKey` throws | No | Unchanged |
| `_harness/ProvisioningTestHarness.psm1` fixture (*"All four jobs, mirroring the real settings files"*) | Comment and content | Add both jobs, so each new query builder is exercised; one new test per branch asserting its `EntityName`, link and operator |
| `provisioning-test-presence`, `provisioning-step-convergence`, `provisioning-syntax` | No by design | No new script; the existing one keeps its test file and its step |

**Words this retires** (`git grep`, 2026-10-22): the script header *"The 6-year paid-grant retention job is NOT
created here"* (rewrite); `config/revitalise-grant-automation-pipeline.yml`, the TST/ACC step description *"The
6-year paid-grant job arrives with the rev_grant table in a later phase"* and the PRD step *"(12m / 6m / orphan
sweep / 90d)"* (rewrite); the harness comment *"All four jobs"* (rewrite); the Dev Summary §3.2 paid-grants row
already tracked by `WI-0142` (rewrite in the same change). §12's *"Recurring bulk-delete jobs ×3"* row is rewritten in
this revision.

**Work-item clauses this overrides** (for pm-agent). None found: no item names the job count, the paid-grant job or
`msdyn_aievent` (grepped `logs/work-items.jsonl`, 2026-10-22). `WI-0142` is related, not overridden.
