### ADR-088: A subject access request is answered by helper mode 3 — one trigger by the process owner, one extract with every store including payments, bank details and QuickBooks; QuickBooks is out of erasure until Finance deletes it

**Status:** `Accepted` (rev 33, approved 2026-10-22, delivery option B) · **Date:** 2026-10-22 · **WBS:** `wbs:0.7` (the SDD places the
helper flow there, SDD §10); the QuickBooks step depends on `wbs:7.1`; one pointer line in the `wbs:0.8` runbook; all
flagged to commercial-agent · **Implements** the reviewer's answers of 2026-10-22, verbatim: *"3. Yes, I like that
design. It should indeed be a manual step by the process owner."*; *"The erasure flow can't delete data from
QuickBooks. That holds financial data and needs to be kept under other legal obligations. After that period has ended
records can be deleted."*; *"Sar include Quickbooksdata is correct."*; *"Finance will delete records after 6 years.
process outside of this solution."*; on the first draft, *"The SAR is part of the workflow.. but is triggered manually
by the process owner. So, not withdrawn from the design."*; on the second draft, *"No, the payments, bank details and
Quickbooks record should all be included in the file. One trigger handling that creates the document. So the file
doesn't even land under the eyes of the process owner. The copy is in the secured SAR folder. It is an accepted risk.
Have two people handle one request is ridiculous."*; at approval, *"Option B. the file is saved in the SAR folder and send protected email. If protected email is not possible then Option A."* and *"Approved."* · **Decides** §5.12 mode 3 (proposed since rev 1) · **Closes by
design** `A-R22`, §4.2's open item and the carried SOFT warning C-DOM-005 · **Records as accepted** `A-R108`.

**Correction record.** Two drafts of this ADR were returned the same day; neither was approved, so nothing approved is
reversed. The first read *"a manual step"* as *"a documented manual procedure, no flow mode"* and withdrew mode 3. The
second restored mode 3 but kept it to what the process owner can read, with Finance and the tenant administrator adding
payments, bank details, QuickBooks and audit history by hand. Every reviewer answer quoted in either draft, marked:

| Reviewer decision | Kept or reversed |
|---|---|
| *"Yes, I like that design. It should indeed be a manual step by the process owner."* | **Kept**: the design is mode 3; the process owner starts it by hand (item 1) |
| *"The erasure flow can't delete data from QuickBooks …"* | Kept (item 6) |
| *"Sar include Quickbooksdata is correct."* | Kept, and now **the flow** reads it (item 4). *Second draft: Finance added it by hand* — reversed by the reviewer |
| *"Finance will delete records after 6 years. process outside of this solution."* | Kept (item 6) |
| *"The SAR is part of the workflow.. but is triggered manually by the process owner. So, not withdrawn from the design."* | Kept (item 1) |
| *"… payments, bank details and Quickbooks record should all be included in the file. One trigger … It is an accepted risk. Have two people handle one request is ridiculous."* | Kept (items 1, 3, 4, 5, 7) |

**Second-draft positions this draft reverses**, each at the reviewer's instruction: (i) *"Nothing the process owner
cannot already see"* (the property) — now the extract holds `REV_FinanceOnly` data; (ii) *"Rejected (c) an audit-read
privilege for the service identity"* — now added; (iii) *"Rejected (d) mode 3 reading `rev_payment` and
`rev_bankaccount`"* — now read; (iv) *"Finance adds QuickBooks by hand"* — now the flow reads it, Finance only as a
fallback; (v) the process owner gathering mailbox content by hand — now the flow searches it.

**Context.** FR-053 requires a complete extract for a named individual. From rev 1 the TAD carried mode 3 of the unbuilt
helper flow only as a proposal, and the reviewer re-accepted the gap at every approval. The helper is still not built
(measured 2026-10-22: no Retention flow among the 13 definitions in source). Volume is about 1,000 applications a year
(NFR-021); a SAR is rare by comparison. The QuickBooks connection is read-only (`ADR-017`) and does not exist in source
yet; its feasibility task `wbs:7.1` has not reported. Nothing said who removes the QuickBooks record when the finance
period ends.

**Decision.** Eight interventions, traced in the same order under Consequences.

1. **Mode 3: one trigger, one extract.** The process owner starts it with *When a row is selected* on `rev_applicant`
   from the Grant Administration app; the flow runs as the service identity, reuses the erasure locate step (a child
   flow shared with mode 2), and writes one extract plus PDF copies to the secured SAR folder. It is **read-only** — no
   delete action, no update of any business table; it logs the run with who started it, when, the applicant reference
   and the stores read (FR-054); its Teams message carries the reference and file name only, never content; under delivery option B (item 7) it sends
   the extract to the requester by protected email. Its own flow
   definition, because a cloud flow has one trigger. Specified in §5.12.
2. **A SAR is access, not erasure.** Nothing is deleted or changed by it. Erasure stays mode 2; when both are asked, the
   extract is sent first.
3. **The flow gathers every store it can reach** (§4.2 item 4): applicant, application, review (without the trustee
   identities), grant, payment and bank account rows, every column; the audit records of each, through an audit-read
   privilege added to `REV Service Automation`; the service mailbox's messages to or from the applicant and referee; the
   signed PDF (library, or DocuSign's combined document where no library copy exists yet). It writes statements for
   `msdyn_aievent`, Teams notifications and the website entry, whose content is already in the extract or out of reach.
4. **QuickBooks is read by the flow through the read-only `ADR-017` connection**, by each payment's `rev_qboreference`.
   The connection does not exist yet and depends on `wbs:7.1`; until it exists the extract's QuickBooks section holds
   the payment rows' own references, amounts and dates and says the QuickBooks copy was not read. Fallback only if the
   requester asks for that copy before then: Finance exports it.
5. **The exposure this creates is accepted** (`A-R108`): finance, bank and audit data in the SAR folder, gathered by a
   service identity whose reach exceeds the person who starts it.
6. **QuickBooks is out of erasure until the finance retention period ends, and then Finance deletes it outside this
   solution.** The QuickBooks financial record (name, amount, date) is the financial record FR-050 retains (Data
   Governance Framework v0.2 §4: *"6 years — Per finance policy"*). An erasure request deletes the Dataverse case as
   mode 2 designs, and the requester is told the QuickBooks record is kept, why, and until when (FR-052). The solution
   writes nothing to QuickBooks and gets no write scope (`ADR-017` unchanged); no bulk-delete job and no flow step
   reaches it.
7. **What stays human, all with the process owner:** the identity check before the run (the flow cannot verify a
   person), which also confirms the email on record; a requester who is a referee, helper, group member or emergency contact (rare). Nobody else
   is in the normal path. **Delivery (decided at approval): option B** — the flow saves the extract in the SAR folder
   and sends it by protected email from the service mailbox; other people's data (Art. 15(4)) leaves unreviewed, accepted
   in `A-R108`. **Option A** — the process owner opens, removes other people's data, sends protected — only if protected
   email is not possible; `A-SAR-4` selects which at build time (§4.2 item 8). *As presented: the judgement and delivery
   were put to the reviewer, with option (a) recommended.*
8. **The procedure document is the process owner's runbook for mode 3** (§4.2 item 11), at
   `docs/training/subject-access-request-procedure.md`.

**Not decided here.** The internal SAR turnaround
(OQ-023, NFR-025) is Revitalise's to set. The website keeps Gravity Forms entries; that copy is outside this
solution, Revitalise's to settle (`A-R107`, closed for this solution). *Rev 34: the evidence log and the packaging of modes 1 and 2 are decided by `ADR-089`.* The
store of the helper's evidence log (FR-054) is decided with the helper's build. How modes 1 and 2 are packaged into flow
definitions is the helper's build decision.

**Consequences, in the order of the Decision.**

1. *User sees:* the process owner selects the applicant, picks the SAR extract from the Flow menu, and gets a Teams
   message naming the file; she does not see its content there. *Cost:* two flow definitions inside the unbuilt helper
   (mode 3, about 42 actions with the option B send; the locate child, about 8, shared with mode 2), one environment variable, one folder per
   environment. **Judgement:** proportionate for nine stores gathered once per request, each in its own scope.
   *Default traced:* if mode 3 is not built by go-live, the runbook covers the stores by hand, which takes several people.
2. *User sees:* nothing changes in any record after a SAR.
3. *User sees:* one file with a section per store, each marked read or not read and why. *Negative:* one new privilege
   (audit read) on the unattended identity, and one new Outlook action; both are unverified (`A-SAR-11`, `A-SAR-12`),
   each with a stated fallback. A column added to the six tables later is gathered without a change to the flow.
4. *User sees:* until `wbs:7.1` delivers the connection, a QuickBooks section built from the payment rows with a "not
   read" line. *Negative:* mode 3 now waits on `wbs:7.1` for that one step; the rest of mode 3 does not.
5. *User sees:* nothing; the risk is in who could open the folder. Controls in `A-R108`.
6. *User sees:* an erasure answer that says the payment record in QuickBooks is kept for six years and then deleted by
   Finance. *Default traced:* if Finance never deletes, the record stays past six years; the solution cannot detect it.
7. *User sees:* the process owner confirms identity and the email on record, starts the run, and the requester
   receives a protected email with the extract (option B); nobody reads the file before it leaves, so other people's data
   in the applicant's own application goes to the requester unreviewed (accepted, `A-R108`). *Default traced:* if
   `A-SAR-4` closes false, mode 3 has no send step, and the process owner opens the file once, removes other people's
   data and sends it protected (option A). *Previously read (as presented): "under the recommended delivery option (a)".*
8. *Default traced:* if the runbook does not exist at go-live, mode 3 can be started without the identity check; that is
   why `wbs:0.7`'s evidence should name the document (pm-agent).

**Rejected.** (a) *A documented manual procedure with no flow mode* (first draft): reversed by the reviewer. (b) *Mode 3
limited to what the process owner can read, with Finance and the tenant administrator adding the rest* (second draft):
reversed by the reviewer — two people per request. (c) *Mode 3 as a choice input on mode 2's trigger*: a SAR run would be
one input away from an erasure, and the read-only property could not be checked from source. (d) *A QuickBooks delete
step*: needs a write scope `ADR-017` refuses, and the reviewer placed the deletion outside this solution. (e) *A
bulk-delete job for QuickBooks*: impossible; a Dataverse bulk delete reaches Dataverse tables only. (f) *A separate
QuickBooks connection for mode 3*: one read-only connection reference serves both the duplicate check and mode 3, so
there is one OAuth grant to govern.

**WBS — flagged to commercial-agent; the scope grew in this draft.** The SDD places *"the cross-system retention/erasure
helper flow"* under `wbs:0.7`, whose contracted description is retention policies, backup, GDPR documentation and DLP,
and whose derived state is complete; no other task names the helper. Mode 3 now adds two flow definitions of about 48
actions, a security-role privilege, a new Outlook action, an environment variable, a folder per environment, and a use
of the QuickBooks connection that `wbs:7.1` must first establish. Whether mode 3, and the helper as a whole, fit
`wbs:0.7` or need a change order, and whether `wbs:7.1`'s connection now serves two purposes within its estimate, is
commercial-agent's to judge (`C-COM-002`); the runbook line in `wbs:0.8` (claimed Done) is the same question. This desk
states no hours.

**Gate interactions.** The helper is unbuilt, so no gate changes today. When mode 3 and the locate child are built, the
flow gates in `config/revitalise-grant-automation-build.yml` that read every flow definition apply: `source-validate`
(its expected flow count rises), `flow-definition-language`, `flow-reads-no-trigger-body`,
`no-hardcoded-environment-values` (the folder path is `rev_SpoSarFolderUrl`), `domain-invariants` (C-DOM-004: the
evidence-log row carries no personal data beyond the reference), `assumption-markers` and `assumption-register`; the
audit privilege meets `role-privilege-ownership`. This ADR prescribes no expression. Actions already in source:
`RecordSelected`, `ListRecords`, `CreateFile`, `PostMessageToConversation`, `GetDocumentsV2`, a child-flow call. New:
SharePoint *Get file content using path* (`A-SAR-6`), *Select* + *Create HTML table* (`A-SAR-7`), the trigger's user
identity (`A-SAR-8`), a QuickBooks read (`A-SAR-10`), `ListRecords` on `audit` (`A-SAR-11`), an Outlook mailbox search
(`A-SAR-12`).

**Words this retires** (`git grep --recurse-submodules`, 2026-10-22, positive control first: *"SAR extract"* found in
this TAD). Three sets: the rev 1 wording, the first draft's (*"documented manual procedure"*, *"No flow mode"*, *"mode 3
is withdrawn"*), and the second draft's (*"Nothing the process owner cannot already see"*, *"Finance adds it by hand"*,
*"does not read `rev_bankaccount` or `rev_payment`"*, *"giving one to the service identity is rejected"*):

| Hit | Mark |
|---|---|
| This TAD: status line, rev 33 entry, reader's note item 5, §4.2, §5.12, §6.6, `A-R22`, `A-R106`, Appendix A FR-053, §7 NFR-025, §12 rows, §12.11, Approval rev 33 status | rewrite (this revision); earlier drafts' wording kept as *Previously read* notes |
| This TAD: Approval section, rev 1 to rev 32 records of C-DOM-005 as accepted | history, kept |
| This TAD: Appendix B row 1 | history, kept; note updated |
| `logs/routing.log` 2026-10-22 lines recording the first and second drafts | history, kept (append-only) |
| `logs/improvement-log.jsonl`: an earlier finding's *expected* field says the knowledge files should cite *"the manual SAR procedure"* | superseded by the findings logged with this revision; improvement-agent reads them together |
| `provisioning/dataverse/ensure-schema.ps1` (*"a documented manual procedure is a design"*) | unrelated, kept |
| `docs/development/revitalise-grant-automation-dev-summary.md`, helper row *"Mode 3 (SAR) has no agreed mechanism"* and the C-DOM-005 row | rewrite, development-agent: mode 3 decided, unbuilt |
| `docs/tests/revitalise-grant-automation-test-report.md`, FR-053, NFR-025, C-DOM-005 and *"SAR path exists"* rows | rewrite at the next test report, test-agent |
| `knowledge/domain/compliance-requirements.md` *"No SAR extract mechanism"* row; `knowledge/domain/regulations.md` Art. 15 and Art. 17 lines; `knowledge/domain/business-rules.md` BR-D04 | rewrite, improvement-agent (findings logged; this desk does not edit `knowledge/`) |
| `docs/architecture/grant-admin-app-architecture.md` and `docs/architecture/revitalise-grant-record-architecture.md` SAR notes | history, kept: both cite the parent's state at their own approval |
| `docs/architecture/trustee-portal-visual-refresh-architecture.md` (*"a SAR extract will silently omit a disclosed redaction"*) | still true: mode 3 reads every column, both raw and `…redacted` |
| `knowledge/domain/glossary.md` *"No SAR or availability SLA exists"* | still true |
| `docs/plans/revitalise-grant-automation-plan.md` *"SAR path exists ✅ FR-053"* | still true |

**Work-item clauses this overrides** (for pm-agent). None: no item names FR-053, a SAR, mode 3, the helper flow or
QuickBooks deletion (grepped `logs/work-items.jsonl`, 2026-10-22). `wbs:7.1` has no work item naming the connection's
second use.

### ADR-089: The whole Retention & Erasure helper — five definitions, a weekly sweep that records what the jobs delete, an erasure mode with a typed confirmation and one hold rule, and an evidence log

**Status:** `Accepted` (rev 34, approved 2026-10-22; D1 to D5 answered, *"D1. Agreed. Will be a platform setting on Docusign"*, *"D2. Agreed. It only erases when final payment is checked."*, *"D3. Option A is agreed."*, *"D4. Thats alright. Process owner will deal with it via the monthly list."*, *"D5. That's alright."*, *"Approved."*) · **Date:** 2026-10-22 · **WBS:** `wbs:0.13`
(`CO-011`, approved 2026-10-22, unbilled; SDD §10 placed the helper under `wbs:0.7`), the whole helper · **Implements** the
reviewer's words of 2026-10-22: *"SAR mode 3 is a change order unbilled... cause it should have been part of the work in a regulated environment."* and *"Definitely include helper modes 1 and 2 in one go."* · **Amends** `ADR-004` (the helper's list) and §5.12; **keeps**
`ADR-088` unchanged.

**Context.** Modes 1 and 2 were drawn in §5.12 from rev 1 at diagram level. Since then the `orphanedApplicants` job
(rev 31) took over one of mode 1's steps, the jobs' run day turned out to depend on when each environment was
provisioned, and the evidence log was never designed (rev 33 *Depends on*). Measured 2026-10-22: no Retention flow in
source; `REV Service Automation` deletes only `rev_provider`; no source flow deletes a Dataverse row, a SharePoint file
or an email, or calls a DocuSign purge.

**Decision.** Nine interventions, traced in the same order under Consequences.

1. **Five definitions** (§5.12.4): sweep, erasure, SAR extract, locate child, snapshot child; about 130 actions.
2. **Mode 1 is weekly with an 8-day look-ahead** and never deletes a Dataverse row (§5.12.1).
3. **Mode 1 records each deletion twice**, *Scheduled* before and *Deleted* after, and flags *Overdue* at 35 days.
4. **One evidence table, `rev_retentionlog`**, for all three modes (§5.12.3).
5. **Mode 2 starts on one applicant with the reference typed** as a confirmation (`A-ERA-1`).
6. **Mode 2's only flow-evaluated hold:** a grant without a recorded final payment (D2, aligned at approval; *as presented: a signed grant not finally paid*).
7. **Mode 2 deletes the applicant row once**; the cascades do the rest (§3.3, `A-ERA-2`).
8. **Mode 2 tells the requester and the DPO** by email from the service mailbox, references and dates only.
9. **Five decisions for the reviewer**, each with this desk's recommendation:
   - **D1 — DocuSign.** Purge envelopes by DocuSign's account-level document retention (completed, declined and
     voided envelopes purged a set number of days after they close; recommended **30**), not by a flow step. The
     signed PDF and certificate live in the library (`A-DS-9`), which modes 1 and 2 delete. Replaces rev 1's *"Purge
     matching DocuSign envelopes"* in mode 1 (adopted from the source, never built). One account serves every
     environment (§12), so the setting applies to test envelopes too. `A-ERA-5`.
   - **D2 — hold rule.** As item 6. Alternative: no flow hold at all, the process owner judges every case.
   **Answers, 2026-10-22:** D1 agreed (a DocuSign platform setting); D2 agreed, *"It only erases when final payment is
   checked."* — the rule now stops on any grant without a final payment, signed or not; D3 option (a); D4 agreed, the
   monthly list; D5 agreed.
   - **D3 — audit history of an erased case.** (a) kept until its 6-year audit retention (§6.5), access-restricted, and
     the requester told so — **recommended**, one person per request; or (b) the tenant administrator deletes the
     case's change history, which keeps audit deletion separate from the service identity (§6.5, C-DOM-012) but adds
     a second person.
   - **D4 — stale open cases.** Mode 1 lists, once a month, applications in statuses 1 to 7 with no contact for 12
     months; the process owner closes them. Alternative: a seventh bulk-delete job with its own rule, which FR-048
     does not state (`A-R110`).
   - **D5 — the evidence log is kept indefinitely** and never bulk-deleted, as it names no data subject. It does name
     the staff member who started an erasure or SAR (rev 33, approved).

**Consequences, in the order of the Decision.**

1. *User sees:* three flows in the Grant Administration app's Flow menu (SAR extract, erasure) and a Monday Teams
   summary. *Cost:* about 80 new actions over three new definitions, one table, two settings keys, privileges.
   **Judgement:** proportionate to a regulated retention duty; each definition does one job, the largest is 42.
2. *User sees:* nothing on most Mondays except counts. *Default traced:* if the setting `RetentionStaleCaseMonths` is
   absent, the stale-case step lists nothing and says *"setting missing"* in the summary — not fail-safe, a blackout,
   stated as one; the settings seed carries 12.
3. *User sees:* an *Overdue* reference in the summary when a job has stopped. The PDF of a deleted case goes within
   about a week of the job run, not on the same night.
4. *User sees:* the DPO and process owner can open the log in the app and see what was deleted, when and under which
   rule, and nothing about the person.
5. *User sees:* a text box asking for the reference; a wrong entry stops the run with nothing changed.
6. *User sees:* a stopped run, a Teams message naming the grant reference, and the requester an email saying the erasure waits for the final payment. *Default traced:* under D2's
   alternative, a case with money committed is erased and the payment has no record in Dataverse.
7. *User sees:* the applicant gone from every view. *Negative:* the unattended identity gains delete on five Tier 4
   tables; mitigated by the typed confirmation, the start-by-person-only trigger and the log.
8. *User sees:* the requester gets one email; the DPO mailbox gets references.
9. *User sees:* depends on the answers; each alternative is stated in item 9.

**Rejected.** (a) *Mode 1 deleting rows itself*: duplicates `ADR-004`'s native jobs. (b) *Mode 1 monthly, aligned to the
jobs*: their day differs per environment. (c) *A "When a row is deleted" trigger to remove the PDF*: the deleted row's
columns, including the PDF URL, are not in that trigger's output as far as this desk can verify, and a cascade delete
of thousands of rows would start thousands of runs. (d) *Erasure as an input on mode 3's trigger*: rejected in `ADR-088`
(c). (e) *A marker column on `rev_application` recording that a snapshot was written*: adds a column and a change to a
built flow to check a failure Failure Alert already reports.

**Reviewer decisions quoted in superseded wording, kept or reversed.** Rev 1's mode 1 steps were adopted from the
source architecture, not decided by the reviewer; the orphan sweep moved to a job by the reviewer-approved rev 31
(kept). No reviewer decision is reversed. D1 replaces an adopted, unbuilt step and is put to the reviewer for that reason.

**WBS.** The reviewer has said `CO-011` covers the whole helper, unbilled. Sizing is commercial-agent's from §5.12.4;
this desk states no hours.

**Gate interactions** (`config/revitalise-grant-automation-build.yml` `steps:`, plus `src/tests/`). `source-validate`
(flow count 13 → 18 with rev 33's two), `flow-definition-language`, `flow-reads-no-trigger-body` (mode 2 reads its
typed input from the trigger — the same class as the check targets; development-agent reads the gate's allow-list
before choosing the expression), `no-hardcoded-environment-values`, `no-hardcoded-thresholds` (12 months is a setting;
the 8-day look-ahead and 35-day overdue are format constants of the weekly schedule, documented as such),
`domain-invariants` (C-DOM-004 on `rev_retentionlog`), `tad-coverage`, `audited-tables`, `field-length-limits`,
`role-privilege-ownership` (delete privileges, `rev_retentionlog`), `assumption-markers`, `assumption-register`,
`assumption-id-collisions` (`A-ERA-1` to `A-ERA-5`, free in both documents, 2026-10-22), and the unit test
`NoTriggerLoop` (no helper definition triggers on a table it writes). This ADR prescribes no expression.

**Words this retires** (`git grep`, 2026-10-22): *"Purge matching DocuSign envelopes"* and *"Delete orphaned Applicant
rows"* in §5.12's diagram (rewrite, this revision); *"verifies a snapshot exists before any record is deleted"* in §5.13
step 3 and Appendix A FR-055 (annotated, this revision); `ADR-004`'s *"DocuSign envelope purge … orphaned-Applicant
sweep"* (history, kept; this ADR amends it); `ADR-088`'s *"decided with the helper's build"* (annotated).

**Work-item clauses this overrides** (for pm-agent). None found: no work item names the helper, FR-049, FR-051 or the
evidence log (grepped `logs/work-items.jsonl`, 2026-10-22).

### ADR-090: Settings carry a Category, the list is sorted by it, and the seed script can update description and category on create-only rows

**Status:** Accepted (rev 35, approved 2026-10-23). **Serves:** `wbs:2.2` (`WI-0151`, `WI-0153`; `CO-012` closed, no change order).

**Context.** The settings table has grown from the first eleven rows to 48 in the settings files (the reviewer counts 50 live).
The process owner finds a setting by scanning a flat list ordered by key. The reviewer asked for a Category column on a new
global choice set so the settings can be grouped in the list. Separately, 16 rows are create-only (`ADR-076` item 6, `ADR-079`
item 6): the seed script never writes them again after creation, so an existing environment would keep an old description and get
no category on exactly the rows Emily edits most.

**Decision (numbered, traced in Consequences in the same order).**

1. **A new global choice set `rev_settingcategory` and a new Choice column `rev_category` on `rev_setting`.** Not required (an
   import or an older row must not fail), audited, not secured. Labels are in the process owner's words and **option values are
   assigned 1 to 8 in the alphabetical order of the labels**, so a sort by value and a sort by label give the same order
   (`A-SETCAT-3`). A later category takes the next value and is allowed to sort by value only.
2. **Every key is placed in exactly one category** (table below).
3. **The Settings list (`AllSettings`) orders by `rev_category`, then `rev_displayname`, then `rev_name`, and shows Category as
   the first column.** The list is the only view of the table and stays the default.
4. **Grouping is offered, not promised.** Grouping into collapsible sections is a feature of the Power Apps grid control (its
   *Enable grouping* property, default No, then each user chooses *Group by* in a column's header menu). A saved view cannot
   carry a group. If a DEV check shows the app's grid offers it and the setting can be exported into solution source, the
   property is turned on for `rev_setting` (**exported from DEV, never hand-authored**, `C-TECH-051`). If not, the list stays
   sorted and filterable and nothing custom is built (the `CO-012` re-price trigger).
5. **The settings file carries `category` on every row, as the label text of the choice** (for example `"category": "Narrative
   scrubbing"`), beside `dataType`, which is also a label. The seed script maps the label to the value through a table next to its
   `$dataTypeMap`, and stops before writing anything if a row has no category or an unknown one (its existing fail-fast).
6. **The seed script's create-only branch gains a metadata path.** For a create-only row that exists, the script updates
   `rev_description` and `rev_category` **by the row's own id** (read from the existing-row probe) and sends no other column. If
   the two values already match it sends nothing. Every other row keeps its upsert, whose body gains `rev_category`.
7. **The repository owns description and category; the process owner owns value.** A description or category edited in the app on
   any seeded row is replaced by the next deploy. The form shows Category read-only to make this visible.

**Categories (50 live keys today: 48 in the settings files and two written by the city register script, marked +; the two rev 34 keys marked * do not exist yet and take the total to 52).**

| Value | Category (what the process owner sees) | Keys |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Acceptance emails and reminders | `AcceptanceEmailApplicant`, `AcceptanceEmailReferee`, `EscalationDays`, `ReminderDays` |
| 2 | Automatic rejection rules | `AmountLimitHolidayAccommodation`, `AmountLimitDayTripsOrOutings`, `AmountLimitActivityOrExperience`, `AmountLimitRespiteCareFacilityStay`, `AmountLimitOther`, `SavingsRuleEnabled`, `PriorFundingRuleEnabled` |
| 3 | Data retention and erasure | `RetentionStaleCaseMonths`*, `ErasureNotificationEmail`* (none exists until the helper's build under `CO-011`) |
| 4 | Lookup lists and wording | `AgeBandMap`, `AgeRangeLabelMap`, `ExceptionalCircumstanceLabelMap`, `EmploymentStatusLabelMap`, `CareHoursBandLabelMap`, `TitleLabelMap`, `ApplicantTypeLabelMap`, `GenderLabelMap`, `EthnicGroupLabelMap`, `LikertResponseLabelMap`, `AgreementResponseLabelMap`, `BreakTypeLabelMap`, `IncomeBandLabelMap`, `HearAboutUsLabelMap`, `ConditionProfileLabelMap`, `CareProvidedTypeLabelMap`, `OtherFundingStatusLabelMap` |
| 5 | Narrative scrubbing | `RedactionNeutralTerms`, `RedactionTitles`, `RedactionNameRules`, `RedactionLabels`, `RedactionConfidenceThreshold` |
| 6 | Postcodes and local authorities | `PostcodeRegionMap`, `LocalAuthorityRegisterMultiAuthorityThresholdPercent`, `CitySourceFile`+, `CitySourceCapturedOn`+ |
| 7 | Round statistics | `RoundStatisticsMoneyMeasureMinimumPopulation`, `RoundStatisticsStaleAfterSeconds`, `RoundStatisticsHistoryStartDate`, `RoundStatisticsHistoryPriorApplicationCount`, `RoundStatisticsMonthlyAnomalyThresholdPercent` |
| 8 | Scoring and eligibility | `KnockoutThreshold`, `BorderlineBandLower`, `BorderlineBandUpper`, `IncomeCeiling`, `IncomeBandUpperBoundMap`, `MaxCircumstanceScore`, `LikertPointMap`, `FeelingScaleInversion` |

Counts live today: 4 + 7 + 0 + 17 + 5 + 4 + 5 + 8 = 50 (48 in the settings files, 2 from the city register script); 52 once the two rev 34 keys arrive. Category 3 has no row until then and is still created, so the helper's build only adds rows. The grouping is by what the process owner is trying to do, not
by which flow reads the key. Two placements are judgement calls she may want changed: `IncomeCeiling` and `IncomeBandUpperBoundMap`
sit under scoring and eligibility, not under rejection rules, because the TAD reads them as the income test (`FR-015`) and not as a
rejection amount limit; and `AgeBandMap` sits with the lookup lists because it translates a stored age into a range label. **The two city provenance keys go in category 6** because they record where
the postcode-to-city list came from (`wbs:4.7`, `CO-007`), the same subject as the postcode and local-authority keys; the other
candidates, lookup lists and wording, hold maps the flows read, and these two are never read by a flow. Because the city
register was paused to V2 only for the local-authority register (the postcode to derived city feature continues), the keys are live.

**How their description and category reach an environment.** `seed-city-settlement-register.ps1` (its provenance block) already
upserts both rows by key on every run with value, data type and description, and they are not create-only. So development-agent adds
`rev_category` (label `Postcodes and local authorities`, mapped to its value through the same label table as `seed-settings.ps1`,
which the two scripts share rather than duplicate) and a plain-language description to that block's upsert; **no metadata-only path is
needed for them**. **NFR-221 (`city-derivation-architecture.md` §5.1) is not breached:** *"seeded once ... never updated thereafter"*
concerns the provenance **value** (file name, delivery date), which stays constant and is rewritten with the same text. Rewriting
the description and category on a re-run changes no fact the requirement protects (which file and which date), and the script's own
header already treats the keyed upsert as idempotent. If the reviewer reads NFR-221 as forbidding any rewrite, the alternative is the
create-only metadata path of item 6 for these two rows, at the cost of a second script reading the file.

**Consequences, traced for the person using the screen (one point per Decision item).**

1. *Choice set and column.* Existing rows have an empty Category until the seed runs. An empty Category sorts to the top of the list
   (assumed, `A-SETCAT-3`) and shows blank: visible, harmless, and cleared by the first deploy. No flow reads the column, so nothing
   changes in scoring, rejection, emails or scrubbing.
2. *Every key placed.* A key added later without a category fails the seed's pre-flight and writes nothing. A key added in the app
   by hand has a blank Category and sits at the top until a developer files it.
3. *The list.* She opens Settings and sees every setting in category order, each category's keys together, Category as the leftmost
   column. She can narrow to one category with the column's filter (the grid's filtering is on by default, `A-SETCAT-1`).
4. *Grouping.* **What she sees is one of two things, decided by the DEV check.** Grouping confirmed: an extra *Group by* item in
   the Category column's menu; choosing it shows eight collapsed sections she opens one at a time; the choice is hers per visit and
   is not saved with the list. Grouping not confirmed: the sorted, filterable list only, and the reviewer is told. This is a
   substitute for what the reviewer asked for (settings "grouped in the view") and is the reviewer's decision at the gate.
5. *The settings file.* A typo in a category label is caught before any row is written. The label list lives in two places (the
   choice set XML and the seed script's table); the Pester test asserts they hold the same eight labels.
6. *The metadata path.* In an existing environment the 16 create-only rows get the new description and category on the next
   deploy and **their value, data type and effective-from date are not in the request**; a value Emily changed survives every
   re-run. The create-only rows still are never created twice. Each write is audited by the table's existing auditing, so the
   description change is visible in the row's history; a re-run that changes nothing writes nothing.
7. *Ownership.* If Emily edits a description on a seeded row, the next deploy puts the repository's text back. That is a change
   from today for the 32 upserted rows too, which already behave this way, and new for the 16 create-only rows.

**Where it is built, and why not elsewhere.** Both new components are created through the Dataverse Web API, not by solution import
(`C-TECH-050`): `ensure-schema.ps1` already reads every `OptionSets/*.xml` and every `Entities/*/Entity.xml` at run time and creates
whatever is missing, so a new option-set file and a new attribute in `rev_setting`'s `Entity.xml` reach each environment through the
existing prerequisite step, in DEV, TST/ACC and PRD, before the solution import (`A-SETCAT-4`). The solution source also carries
the new choice set (`Solution.xml` root component type 9), the new column, the list change and the form field, as for every
other component.

**Seeding path, step by step (for development-agent; the shape, not the code).**
1. Probe the row by key, selecting its id, description and category (replaces the existing name-only probe).
2. Row missing: create it with value, data type, description, category and effective date, as today.
3. Row exists and not create-only: upsert, as today, with `rev_category` added to the body.
4. Row exists and create-only: if description and category both already equal the file, report `EXISTS — left unchanged
   (createOnly)`; otherwise update by the row's id with a body of exactly `rev_description` and `rev_category`, and report `EXISTS —
   description and category updated (createOnly; value untouched)`. An update by id cannot create a row, so a row deleted between
   probe and write fails visibly instead of appearing without a value.
5. Pester: a fixture create-only row with a changed value; assert the update body has no `rev_value`, `rev_datatype`,
   `rev_displayname` or `rev_effectivefrom` key; assert no POST; assert a re-run with matching text sends no write.

**Gate interactions** (`config/revitalise-grant-automation-build.yml` `steps:`, plus `src/tests/`). `field-length-limits` (the
rewritten descriptions stay within the column's 2000, and the seed's own 1000-character comment in `settings-rows.notes.md` is
unchanged; development-agent re-runs it), `source-validate` and the provisioning Pester suite (`DataverseScripts.Tests.ps1`,
`SeedSettings.Tests.ps1`: the option-set and attribute counts these suites and `verify-source-derived-test-counts.py` assert will
move by one choice set and one column), `verify-derived-counts` (row counts claimed in documents; provisional while `WI-0150`
edits the same files, see the gate output), `audited-tables`, `assumption-markers`, `assumption-register`,
`assumption-id-collisions` (`A-SETCAT-1` to `A-SETCAT-5`, free in both documents, 2026-10-23), `tad-coverage`. No flow expression
is prescribed, so the flow-language gates do not apply.

**Assumptions opened (all `OPEN`, each with a §12 verification).**

| Id | Claim | How it is closed |
|---|---|---|

Not exercised in this app | DEV: configure `rev_setting` in the maker portal, open the list as Emily's role, group by Category; screenshot |

**Open for the reviewer (lettered; the first is the real choice).**
- **(A) Grouping.** Accept sort plus filter now with grouping conditional on a DEV check, or require grouping and accept a custom control (a re-price, outside `wbs:2.2`). *Recommended: accept.*
- **(B) Categories.** Are the eight names and the two judgement-call placements right for Emily?

## 11. Risks & Mitigations

R1–R9 are the risks *to individuals* adopted from SDD §7.7 (DPIA §6–§7). A-R10 onward are
**architecture-level risks identified during this intake** and are new to the document set.

| Risk | Likelihood | Impact | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|---|
| **R1** A trustee identifies an applicant from data that should be redacted | Low (after controls) | High | Column security profile applied below the app layer (§6); redaction fails closed (§5.5); trustee role has no export privilege; print/pack routes render only permitted columns |
| **R2** Special-category health data exposed to someone without a need to see it | Low | High | Tier 4 columns in `REV_TrusteeRestricted`; Finance role has no Application privilege; four narrow persona roles; role changes notified to the DPO |
| **R3** An applicant wrongly rejected by the automated score without meaningful human review | **Medium — pending DPO (OQ-005)** | High | FR-018 override, FR-019 Borderline routing, FR-022 withhold-on-missing-answer; thresholds in `rev_setting` so auto-reject can be routed through the process owner as a **configuration change** if the DPO requires it. **Rev 26 (`ADR-079`):** four more rules now reject automatically (4 of 63 Round 4 applications on financial grounds, SDD A-10 Finding 2). Emily checks every auto-reject with all its reasons (reviewer, 2026-10-19). A switch or a limit can turn a rule **off**; no setting routes a rule's cases to review instead, so if the DPO requires review rather than rejection (OQ-005) that is a flow change, not a configuration change |
| **R4** Health free-text kept longer than necessary on granted records | **Medium — DPO decision open (OQ-006)** | Medium | `rev_narrativeraw` is a distinct column, so early redaction is a configuration change, not a rebuild |
| **R5** Bank or payment details accessed outside the Finance role | Low | High | Table-level denial to `REV Admin` **plus** `REV_FinanceOnly` column profile — defence in depth |

## 12. Provisioning & External Dependencies

Every component that **cannot ship inside the solution**. Scope `tenant` → `tenant_prerequisites` block in
`config/revitalise-grant-automation-pipeline.yml`, gated `APPROVE TENANT`; scope `per-env` → `post_deploy`.
All scripts must be idempotent, check-before-create, and report `CREATED` / `EXISTS` / `FAILED` per resource
(C-TECH-042, development-agent / pipeline-agent scope).

| Item | Type | Tool / Script | Scope | Gate |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `REV-GrantApplications-DEV` environment security group | Entra ID security group | `provisioning/entra/` — Microsoft Graph PowerShell | tenant | `APPROVE TENANT` |
| `REV-GrantApplications-ACC` environment security group — **new, required by the three-environment topology (ADR-006)** | Entra ID security group | `provisioning/entra/` — Graph PowerShell | tenant | `APPROVE TENANT` |
| `REV-GrantApplications-PRD` environment security group | Entra ID security group | `provisioning/entra/` — Graph PowerShell | tenant | `APPROVE TENANT` |
| `REV-PP-GrantApplications-Admins-ACC`, `REV-PP-GrantApplications-Service-ACC` (TST/ACC), `REV-PP-GrantApplications-Admins-PRD`, `REV-PP-GrantApplications-Service-PRD` (PRD) role groups — **Phase 1 scope only; `Finance`/`Trustees` role groups are not created in this phase, no Phase 1 table is reachable by either persona.** Already created manually by the reviewer on 2026-08-14 | Entra ID security groups (4) | `provisioning/entra/` — Graph PowerShell | tenant | `APPROVE TENANT` |
| **`svc-grantautomation@revitalise.org` service account: creation, licences, MFA, scoped Conditional Access exception** | Entra ID user + CA policy | **Manual — Wanstor (WBS 0.3)** | tenant | `APPROVE TENANT` — ⚠️ **OUTSTANDING AND BLOCKING (SDD OQ-018, risk A-R13)** |
| **`rev-grantautomation-deploy-dev` / `-tstacc` / `-prd` app registrations (3) + a Dataverse application user for each in ITS OWN environment only** — **CHANGED 2026-08-12 (ADR-007/ADR-021).** Replaces the single shared `rev-grantautomation-deploy`. **The row above needs a Dev Summary §10 register row, and this document deliberately does not
allocate its id (added rev 7).** `development-agent` opens it, taking a **fresh** id and checking it
against the register before use — test-report **D-01** is an `A-FIN` id already carrying two
different meanings, and `verify-assumption-markers.py` cannot see that class of collision because it
only checks that the id appears at the target.

**These can be authored blind, and the mitigation is the first-environment sweep, not care**
(A-R59). Every row closes in one pass against DEV before the first deploy — not one import failure
at a time. This project has already paid fifteen import attempts for the alternative.

**One contract is genuinely unknown and is named rather than assumed:** whether a model-driven app
whose every bound column is column-secured renders its forms **empty** for a user with no profile
membership, or **errors**. §6.2.1 assumes empty fields, from how column security behaves elsewhere
in this solution. It is a V4 observation, and it is recorded as an assumption, not a fact.

architectural decision still open.** → **Closed 2026-09-25 (rev 10): Entra client credentials, by reviewer statement.** **Unchanged and still outstanding externally:** DPO decisions
SDD OQ-004/005/006 (ADR-002 conditional), the WBS 0.3 service account with Wanstor (risk A-R13), and the

## Appendix C — Intake field map: the website's native payload → Dataverse (rev 9, `wbs:4.2`)

**This appendix is the `wbs:4.2` field-mapping deliverable.** It supersedes the payload-contract
half of `docs/development/revitalise-grant-automation-form-validation-spec.md` (§8 there, *"The payload
contract as it really is"*). That section described a contract of our own, which no sender sends.
The spec's §4–§7 remain the record of the live form's questions and conditional logic. `wbs:4.2`'s
own description requires *"Review with Emily"*: this appendix is that review's input, and it has not
yet been reviewed with her.

**Source:** `docs/Import/2026-09-25-website-intake-payload-sample.json` — one test entry (form 3,
entry 1895), sanitised on intake. **Sender's rules:** `docs/Import/2026-09-25-alex-intake-payload-covering-note.md` (rev 10; E2 for
every route). **E1 for the keys and for the value shapes on the routes it took.**
It is one instance, and it proves nothing about routes left empty (§12.3 `A-INT-06`, `A-INT-07`).
Column facts are from `Entities/rev_applicant/Entity.xml` and `Entities/rev_application/Entity.xml`,
and option values from `OptionSets/*.xml`, all read 2026-09-25.

**Internal name** is the property `Normalise_payload` emits (`ADR-051` item 2). Where one exists, it is
the name the flow already uses today, so downstream actions keep their meaning. **Rule** refers to
§C.2. **Class**: `SC` = in `constraints/domain/special-category-register.yml` `columns:`; `PII` = in
its `pending_adjudication:` block (identifying, secured); `—` = neither.

### C.1a Always-shown questions — the scope of key-drift detection (`ADR-051` item 5)

The questions every applicant sees on every route. This is derived from the form-validation spec §5's conditional rules and the 2026-09-11 capture (E3), and verified by the route test entries (`A-INT-06`). Only these keys go into `Expected_payload_keys`:

`grant_terms_and_conditions`, `name_title`, `name_first`, `name_last`, `address_street_address`, `address_town_city`, `address_postcode`, `preferred_contact_method`, `age_confirmation`, `age_range`, `are_you`, `overall_how_satisfied_are_you_with_your_life_nowadays`, the seven `please_say_what_best_describes_…` keys, the three `thinking_about_the_last_year_…` keys, `do_you_currently_receive_any_means_tested_benefits`, `please_briefly_explain_why_youre_unable_to_fund_this_break_yourself`, `type_of_break`, `location_or_activity_name`, `provisional_date`, `accommodation_or_activity_cost`, `travel_costs`, `other_costs`, `amount_requesting_from_revitalise`, `are_you_receiving_funding_from_any_other_sources_for_this_break`, `id_like_to_make_an_exceptional_funding_request`, `please_briefly_explain_how_this_break_would_benefit_you`, `is_this_part_of_a_group_trip`, `have_you_received_funding_from_us_before`, `how_did_you_hear_about_us`, `would_you_like_the_form_posted_to_you`, `gender`, `ethnic_group`.

Every other key may be absent without comment.
(helper name parts, and the seven two-week items by suffix). Every metadata key is in §C.6. A Pester
assertion over the fixture should enforce this count, so a key added by the website is noticed.

### C.2 Type rules (applied inside `Normalise_payload`, configuration-free)

| Rule | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| **NOT ANSWERED** (rev 10, applies before every other rule) | key absent, `null`, `""` after trim, `[]` | null. The column is not written, whatever shape the sender uses (`ADR-051` item 11) |
| TEXT | string | `trim()`; `""` → null |
| **TEXT, structured columns only** (rev 13, `ADR-053` point 4, `IMP-0934`) — the closed list `ADR-053` point 1 classifies as structured (`rev_applicant`'s name/contact/address columns, `rev_helperemail`, `rev_helperphone`) | string, trimmed length exceeds the column's literal `MaxLength` | null plus a note naming the field and the limit — the same shape as an unparseable number (item 10) — instead of the write failing at `Create_application`/`Refresh_existing_applicant`. Never fires on a Memo column: every column that could plausibly overflow is Memo after `ADR-053` |
| BOOL | JSON boolean | as sent |
| GATED | JSON boolean + the routing answer | the boolean when `is_someone_helping_you_complete_this_application` is `"Yes"`, otherwise null. The consent date is `received_at` when the boolean is true, otherwise null |
| YESNO | `"Yes"` / `"No"` / `""` | true / false / null; any other string → null plus a note |
| MONEY | numeric string | strip `£` and spaces, then `isFloat(x,'en-GB')` → `float(x,'en-GB')`; `""` → null; non-numeric → null plus a note |
| INT | numeric string | `isInt(x)` and 0 ≤ x ≤ 10 → `int(x)`; otherwise null plus a note |
| JOIN | two TEXT parts | `trim(concat(first,' ',last))`; empty → null |
| MAP / MULTI | label / array of labels | `ADR-051` items 3 and 4, via §C.4 |

### C.3 What the old contract wrote that this payload cannot supply

| Old contract field | Column | What happens now |
|---|---|---|
| `date_of_birth` | `rev_applicant.rev_dateofbirth` | Never supplied, because the form has no such question. The column stays empty, and its requirement level becomes None (`ADR-051` item 9) |
| `first_name`, `last_name`, `postcode`, `submission_id` | as before | Supplied under `name_first`, `name_last`, `address_postcode`, `id` |
| every `*_consent_date` (5) | `rev_*consentdate` | The payload has no timestamps. Each date is `received_at` (the receipt time the flow already writes to `rev_submittedon`), written when the consent is true |

### C.5 Validation and rejection

- **Caller gates:** unchanged (trigger authentication plus the `x-rev-client-id` header, `ADR-011`).
- **Reject with 400** (logged via `rev_errorlog` and alerted — the existing path) **only** when `id`,
  `name_first`, `name_last` or `address_postcode` is empty after trimming.
- **Everything else is accepted.** Each defect becomes a column left empty plus one sentence on
  `rev_intakereviewnote` (`ADR-051` item 10). **What the process owner sees:** the application
  appears as normal, the affected field is blank, and the note says which field and why. The website
  gets 201.
- **Replay:** an `id` already held returns 200 with the original reference and writes nothing
  (unchanged).

### C.6 Not transferred — generated by the form or the plugin, not entered by the applicant (`ADR-051` items 7 and 12)

**Metadata keys:** `form_id`, `post_id`, `date_created`, `date_updated`, `is_starred`, `is_read`,
`source_url`, `currency`, `payment_status`, `payment_date`, `payment_amount`, `payment_method`,
`transaction_id`, `is_fulfilled`, `created_by`, `transaction_type`, `status`, `source_id`, and
`ip`/`user_agent` (removed from the fixture, but sent by the website). **Also:** the form-calculated
`total_estimated_cost`, and the hidden fixed-value `address_country` (and `address_state_province`
unless Alex confirms it is shown).

None of these is read into any column. All are hidden in run history once `A-INT-01` holds.

- **The single exception is the entry `id`.** It is kept, as `rev_sourcesubmissionid`, only because
  it is the technical duplicate key (§4.1). No persona is shown it and nothing reports on it.
- **FR-008's submission timestamp is met by the flow's own receipt time.** `received_at = utcNow()`
  is evaluated once in `Normalise_payload` and written to `rev_submittedon`, as the flow already
  does. It is never taken from `date_created`, even though the covering note confirms that is UTC.
  The two differ by the webhook's transit time, in seconds.

The first-time writes to existing columns (`rev_careprovidedtype` and its two free-text siblings) land on columns the register already adjudicates |

### C.9 `CASCADE: SPEC_GAP` — the requirement text rev 10 needed from plan-agent

**✅ Resolved 2026-09-25 by SDD Amendment A-08** (FR-083–FR-093, §7.1c, OQ-051–OQ-053). Kept as the record of what was asked for.

No FR text is written here. Each item names what the SDD lacks, and the reviewer's instruction is
the requirement it must state.

1. **An intake transfer rule as a requirement.** Store every value the applicant enters, transfer
   nothing the form or plugin generates, with the entry id as the single exception. This amends
   FR-007's *"create a grant application record"*, which says nothing about which data.

   classification row.

   **§7.1/§7.1a classification rows (C-DOM-001), the Art. 9 condition for processing (C-DOM-002),
   and a DPIA line**. Plus a decision on **trustee visibility** — raw, redacted counterpart (the
   ADR-027 pattern), or none. That decision sizes Automation #5 work.
4. **`rev_someonehelping`, `rev_provisionaldate`, `rev_otherfundingstatus`:** an FR or FR amendment
   each, and §7.1 rows. `rev_provisionaldate` touches **FR-001** (*"preferred holiday dates"*) and
   EF-09. `rev_otherfundingstatus` touches FR-035's financial-context list.
5. **FR-001 and FR-027 name a date of birth** (FR-001 as a mandatory field; FR-027 as the source of
   the age range) **that the live form does not collect.** `ADR-051` item 9 has relaxed the column,
   but the requirement text still says otherwise.

   shown.~~ **Closed rev 17:** the reviewer ruled the fields are not on the form; the columns are removed.
